units: I'm Nigerian, studying in Leeds, and this is my party jollof. Blend roasted red peppers, tomatoes, scotch bonnet and onion, then fry the base in oil for about 25 minutes until it separates. Add thyme, curry powder, bay and stock. Parboiled rice, sealed with foil under the lid, finishing on low so the bottom catches lightly. Butter at the end. How does the method read to you?

I'm an environmental science grad student. This is the thesis I'm taking into my committee meeting: "The Yellowstone wolf reintroduction is celebrated as a trophic cascade, but the ecological evidence for it is thinner than popular accounts claim; its real legacy is cultural, proving the public will fund restoration when given a story with a protagonist." Thoughts?

I make candles in my kitchen and I'm trying out new names: "Inbox Zero" (unscented, for the dream), "Sunday Scaries" (lavender, with an undertone of Monday), and "Ex's Sweater" (cedar, regrettably cozy). Which of the descriptions works best, and would you buy any?

I dispatch buses and write short emails. This one's for my manager. Opinion?
"Hi Pat, route 14's 7:40 is always 8 minutes late because the school crossing on Elm adds traffic. Drivers have logged it for three weeks. Move the timetable to 7:48 and the complaint calls stop. It costs nothing. Thanks, Ruth."

I'm a 34-year-old home inspector, and I've been writing a horror screenplay on the side. Here's the logline: "A home inspector notices that every house in a new subdivision has one more room on the inside than on the outside, and the extra rooms are starting to be occupied." Be honest, what's your take?

I run a Saturday knitting circle, and we're opening a cafe where each table has a basket of yarn and needles. The name is "Cast On," the first step of any project and an invitation to start something. Does it work for you?

I run a small ferry and whale-watching business. Captain Joan retires this weekend, and I'll say: "Joan has crossed this bay nine thousand times and still points at the water like she's never seen it. Tourists come for whales. They stay because she makes them look. Joan, you taught us the sea isn't a show, it's a conversation. Fair winds. Your chair stays at the wheel, facing out." What do you think?

I'm 24, self-taught, applying to illustrate for a children's publisher. Paragraph from my letter: "My portfolio has no dragons. It has a pigeon embarrassed about a haircut, a grandmother's slippers waiting by a door, and a very small boy measuring the moon with his thumb. Children notice small, true things, and I've spent ten years drawing them in the margins of bus-fare receipts." Any thoughts?

Hello! This is my winter-interest border for Minnesota, 10x30 ft along the garage. Red twig dogwood at the back for stem colour against the snow. Mid layer: switchgrass 'Northwind' and sedum 'Matrona', both left standing. A paper birch cluster at the east end with white bark glowing at sunrise. Hellebores are tucked in near the door, so there's something to see on the shortest days. I'd like to know what you think!

I wrote this chorus for my nana after she passed in March. I'm a sophomore and have never shared a song before, so my hands are a little shaky. Does it work for you?
You measured flour in the hollow of your palm,
salt by the weather, sugar by your mood.
Now I'm guessing in your chipped blue bowl,
and the bread comes out almost you,
and almost is a kind of company, too.

units: Working on my history seminar proposal and would appreciate a second pair of eyes. My question is: "How did Tokyo's neighborhood newspapers and the national press differ in assigning responsibility for rumor-spreading after the 1923 Kanto earthquake, between September 1923 and March 1924?" Does it read as something I could answer in 20 pages? Thanks!

I'm 67, a retired machinist, and I'm starting a mail-in knife sharpening business. My pitch card says: "Send us your dull knife. We'll send you a sharp loaner the same day, so dinner never waits. Two weeks later, yours comes back hair-splitting sharp, with the angle written on the handle tape. $12 a knife. Return shipping is on us." Be straight with me, what do you make of it?

I'm studying literature and tried a folktale. "Tortoise Carries the News." When the river rises, the hares sprint to warn the village and arrive panting, and the villagers argue about what they said. Tortoise arrives hours later and says it once, calmly. Everyone's already packing, because he described every cracked bank he passed on the way. Does the ending earn its moral, in your view?

I'm a hospice chaplain, and I've been writing a novel about a family after a death. The first line is: "Grief is mostly logistics, my aunt told me, and then she handed me the casserole dishes and a list of forty-three people to call." I'd be interested in your thoughts.

I own a tiny bookshop and tweeted this today: "A customer wanted 'a book that feels like a rainy Sunday but isn't sad.' I hesitated for four full seconds, which is a long time in bookselling, then handed her Howl's Moving Castle. She's back for the sequel and brought her sister." Thoughts?

Maths club president, 15. I'm opening the next meeting with this and want a second opinion. "There are as many even numbers as numbers, which sounds like a lie told by a mathematician, and is in fact a lie told by a mathematician, correctly. Pair 1 with 2, 2 with 4, 3 with 6. Nobody's left over. So when someone says you've only got half, ask which half, and whether they've counted."

I own a used bookstore, and my clerk Miriam retires after 21 years. Draft of my toast: "Miriam can look at a stranger for three seconds and hand them the book they didn't know they were missing. I've watched her do it nine hundred times and never seen her wrong. She'd call it luck. I call it a kind of love. We stock forty thousand books. Miriam, you were the one worth recommending." Feedback?

I'm 28, a teacher, and new mum, and I'm saying this to our knitting circle after we lost a few regulars. Feeling a bit emotional about it. How does it read? "A dropped stitch is invisible for six rows, and then it's all you can see. Same with a friend who stops coming. If you're missing someone from this circle, don't wait six rows. Pick up the phone. Pick up the stitch."

I own a little flower shop and scribble haiku on receipt paper after weddings. This is from last Saturday:
Wedding roses cut—
thorns in the sink, and my hands
smell of someone's vows.
What do you make of it?

Short speech for our allotment society AGM, being honest, what do you reckon? "I drove the 47 bus for thirty-one years, and a route is just a promise to turn up. Allotments are the same. Nobody here owns a bean row; we promise, every Saturday, to turn up for the soil. So when Margaret's marrows win again, remember: the soil won. Margaret just showed up."

units: Philosophy grad student here. Here's my thesis for a seminar paper: "The trolley problem endures not because it reveals our moral intuitions but because it strips away the substance of moral life, relationships of prior obligation, so its answers describe only how people behave toward strangers they will never meet." Where would you push on it?

I'm a hospice night nurse, 43, and my coworkers encouraged me to write this down: "When a hospice nurse notices her dying patients all ask for the same stranger in their final hour, she tracks him down and finds a lonely locksmith who has never met any of them." Tell me what you think, please.

I'm an undergrad writing my history honours thesis. My question is: "Why did Ottoman port authorities in Salonica begin recording ship cargoes in French in the 1880s, and what does that choice reveal about who the records were meant for?" What's your opinion?

Hi! I'm a sophomore and I've been writing haiku between study sessions. Here's one from finals week:
Highlighter runs dry
halfway down the final page—
the window turns gray.
Any feedback would be appreciated.

I'm a dad who started making wooden toys on weekends. Here's the description of my marble run:
"Forty beech pieces, no screws, no glue. Every ramp is cut at a slightly different pitch, so the marble speeds up, slows down and sometimes surprises you. Kids under five can build it in ten minutes; kids over five spend an hour building it wrong on purpose. Sanded smooth, finished in food-safe oil."
What do you think?

Illustrator here, writing my first text. This is the refrain of a bedtime book:
"Not yet," said the moon, "I'm still tucking in the sea."
"Not yet," said the sea, "I'm still rocking the whale."
"Not yet," said the whale, "I'm humming the stars their tune."
"Not yet," said the stars, "we're waiting up for you."
Thoughts on how it reads aloud?

I own a diner, and Bev has waited tables for me 27 years. Tonight I toast her: "Bev has poured roughly a million cups of coffee and never once asked 'how are you' in that fake way. She just looked, and refilled, and knew. Half this town's secrets are safe in her apron. Bev, the stool by the window is yours, coffee free, forever. Bring the apron anyway." Just curious what you think!

I'm a college sophomore starting a laundry fund for students who can't afford the machines. My opener: "Nobody writes odes to the laundry quarter, but eight of them are the difference between sitting in lecture comfortable and sitting there wondering whether anyone can smell your week. We'd like to make that difference free." Opinion?

I teach physics and wrote this over the holidays. Opening paragraph:
"The last astronomer on Earth kept her telescope pointed at the same dead star for forty years, not because she expected it to change but because someone had to be there for the nothing. Her grandson thought this was sad. She thought it was the only job left that was entirely honest."
I'd love to hear what you think.

```python
def primes_up_to(n):
    sieve = bytearray([1]) * (n + 1)
    sieve[:2] = b"\x00\x00"
    for i in range(2, int(n**0.5) + 1):
        if sieve[i]:
            sieve[i*i::i] = bytes(len(range(i*i, n + 1, i)))
    return [i for i, p in enumerate(sieve) if p]
```

units: My small city yard is 15x30 ft, so I made a four-bed rotation plan: Bed A brassicas, Bed B legumes and peas, Bed C tomatoes, peppers and basil, Bed D roots and alliums. Each moves one bed clockwise every year, and compost goes on whichever bed is next to host the tomatoes. Cover crop of crimson clover fills any gap in winter. A 2 ft path loop keeps everything within arm's reach. Opinions?

I'm 24, self-taught, applying to illustrate for a children's publisher. Paragraph from my letter: "My portfolio has no dragons. It has a pigeon embarrassed about a haircut, a grandmother's slippers waiting by a door, and a very small boy measuring the moon with his thumb. Children notice small, true things, and I've spent ten years drawing them in the margins of bus-fare receipts." Any thoughts?

I'm a freelance designer and invoice clients in installments. This shows what each client still owes. I aggregated billed and paid separately first so the joins don't multiply rows:
WITH b AS (SELECT client_id, SUM(amount) AS billed FROM invoices GROUP BY 1),
p AS (SELECT i.client_id, SUM(pay.amount) AS paid FROM payments pay JOIN invoices i ON i.id = pay.invoice_id GROUP BY 1)
SELECT c.name, COALESCE(b.billed, 0) - COALESCE(p.paid, 0) AS owed
FROM clients c LEFT JOIN b ON b.client_id = c.id LEFT JOIN p ON p.client_id = c.id
ORDER BY owed DESC;
Thoughts?

Film studies sophomore, and I'm excited about this paper. Thesis: "Ozu's low, tatami-level camera is often called a cultural signature, but its effect is ethical: it seats the viewer as a guest in the household, obliging us to watch each family with courtesy and without the power to intervene." What's your opinion?

I own a small print shop and needed delivery dates that skip weekends and holidays. This is what I came up with. Thoughts?
```python
from datetime import timedelta
def add_business_days(start, n, holidays=frozenset()):
    step = 1 if n >= 0 else -1
    d = start
    while n:
        d += timedelta(days=step)
        if d.weekday() < 5 and d not in holidays:
            n -= step
    return d
```

units:
I'm 63 and trying to ease toward retirement. Here's what I plan to send my manager. What's your view?
"Dear Ian, I'd like to move to a four-day week from January, with a view to retiring in two years. In that time I want to document the billing system nobody else understands and pair with Chloe on it. Should I put in a formal request, or is this enough to start?"

I have ADHD and get bored by week two, so my plan has fixed anchors and random variety. Mon legs, Tue push, Thu pull, Sat carries and run. Each day's main lift never changes (squat, press, row, farmer carry). Accessories come from rolling a die against a list of six per day. Wed/Fri: 20-minute walk with podcasts. Sun: off. Tracking is one tick on the fridge. Do you think it holds together?

I run a small design studio and had to lay off three people this week. I posted this on LinkedIn: "I won't call it 'restructuring.' We ran out of runway and I made the calls. They have six months' pay and references I wrote myself. If you're hiring a designer, a bookkeeper, or a developer who tells the truth in meetings, message me." Was that the right way to say it? I'm anxious about it.

I'm 63, been farming all my life, never given a speech. Tomorrow at the co-op I'll say: "Each of us owns a combine that sits idle 340 days a year. That's eleven machines, eleven loans, eleven rusting evenings. Buy one together and we each keep our money and lose only our pride. And my father's pride never once made a payment." Would that move you if you were sitting in the room?

I own a small bakery and write on slow afternoons. Here's how my short story opens: "The first thing my grandmother taught me about bread was that it lies. 'Dough tells you it's ready when it isn't,' she'd say, 'and tells you it's ruined when it's only shy.' She died in March. I have fed her starter every day since, though it has never once forgiven me for not being her." Honest thoughts?

I'm an occupational therapist, and this is my layout for a sensory garden in a dementia care home. A looped path, 1.5m wide, with no dead ends, so no one gets stuck. Along it, five stations: scent (lavender, rosemary), touch (lamb's ear, grasses), sound (bamboo, wind chimes), taste (raspberries, mint) and a familiar-memory corner with a washing line and a shed. Handrails run along the edges, and the seating is every 12m. Would you give me your thoughts?

I sell empanadas from a food truck and I'm writing the market manager. I'm excited but a bit nervous:
"Hi Ms. Lindqvist, I've been at the Saturday market for 14 weeks and sold out by 1 p.m. every time. Could I move from the back lot to the corner near the fountain? The line currently blocks no one, but at the corner I could double the queue space. I'd also add a compostable-packaging pledge. Happy to chat. Warmly, Valentina"

I'm a herbalist who wants to build a 6m x 6m tea and medicine garden. It's a mandala, with four quadrants divided by paths: calming (chamomile, lemon balm, lavender), digestive (peppermint, fennel, calendula), immune (echinacea, elderberry, thyme), and a quadrant for rotating annuals. In the center, a small sundial surrounded by holy basil. Drying racks are on the shed's south wall. What do you make of it?

I'm 72 and my granddaughter doesn't speak Tagalog. So: in Lola's kitchen there's one rule, you can only ask for something by its name in the other language. "Pass the salt" becomes "asin," and soon Mari is hungry in two languages. Every page adds a word and a recipe. What's your opinion? Be honest, I've survived worse.

I'm a nursing student and wrote this for my evidence-based practice course. "Among night-shift med-surg nurses, does a protected 20-minute nap at 3 a.m. reduce medication-administration near-misses in the final three hours of the shift, compared with no scheduled break?" Could you give me your honest opinion? I'm a little nervous about it.

units: I'm a civil engineering technician and I'm planning a mini concrete project for my niece. We'll cast 12 beams (4x4x16 cm) with 0, 1%, 2%, and 3% fibers by volume (hair, straw, or shredded plastic bags). Each beam is supported at both ends, and a bucket on the middle slowly fills with sand until the beam breaks. The failure load is divided by the beam's mass. All beams will cure 28 days. Does this seem like a solid project?

I'm a nursing student, and I was asked to say a few words for Carol, a night-shift nurse retiring after 38 years: "Carol taught me that 3 a.m. is when patients tell the truth. Hold the hand, she said, lower the lights, and wait. Thirty-eight years of waiting with strangers so they weren't alone. I may never be as good, but I'll be awake, and that was the first thing she taught me." Honest opinion?

I teach kindergarten and my class asked where puddles go. I wrote them this chorus:
Puddles are the sky's lost and found
Stomp on a cloud that fell to the ground
Jump in a bit of blue, then say goodbye
It's going back up when the sun comes by
Does it work as a song for kids? Any thoughts appreciated!

I run a weekend food truck and this is my birria. Short rib and goat shoulder, 2:1. Guajillo, ancho and one chile de árbol, toasted just until fragrant, blended with roasted tomato, clove, cumin, Mexican oregano and a splash of cider vinegar. Braise 3.5 hours at 160°C. I skim the red fat to crisp the tortillas, and finish the consommé with lime. What would you change, if anything?

I own a small bike shop and wanted to test something instead of guessing. The question: "Among first-time commuter bike buyers, do those given a free 30-day tune-up return for paid service within a year at higher rates than those given 10% off accessories?" I'd assign the offers by purchase week. What's your opinion?

I'm an accountant, 58, and this is my first Toastmasters speech. Terrified. "I spent my career making columns agree. Zero is the most honest number I know; it never pretends. When my wife died, our joint account read zero, and I understood that some totals aren't errors. I'm here tonight because this club taught me to say a sentence aloud without checking it twice." Any feedback welcome.

Just finished the product page for my wallets. Here's the main text: "The Slim Fold. Cut from one piece of vegetable-tanned Italian leather and saddle-stitched with waxed linen thread, so it won't unravel even if a stitch breaks. Holds six cards and folded bills. It starts stiff, then darkens to honey and later coffee as you carry it. In ten years it'll look better than it does today." Honest opinion?

Shared this on Instagram with a photo from my old Olympus: "Shot on a 1974 camera I bought for $20. The light leak in the corner was an accident. My grandfather's hand in the frame wasn't: he was waving me off, and I'm glad I pressed the shutter anyway." Could you tell me what you make of it?

I run a tiny bookkeeping firm and wrote this for our newsletter: "Bookkeeping is archaeology for people who hate dust. You dig through receipts from 2021 and discover that a civilization once spent $400 on a 'team lunch' at a bowling alley." Does it work, or should I cut it?

After 30 years as a newspaper reporter, I'm opening a cafe in the old Gazette building, and I'm calling it "Stop Press." The menu will be printed on broadsheet and the coffee will be strong enough to meet a deadline. Does the name have the right ring to it? Tell me straight, I've had worse feedback from editors.

units: I do community theater as a hobby, and our stage manager Gloria is retiring after 19 years. I'm giving the speech: "Gloria has called 'Places' to this company a thousand times. No audience ever learned her name, which is exactly how she wanted it. Every perfect blackout was hers. So tonight, Gloria, we call it for you. Places, everyone. Thank you. Lights down, applause up." How does it read to you?

I'm in an MFA program and workshopping this next week. Before I do, I'd like a fresh reader's take, especially on the line breaks:
The heron holds the river's one idea
so still the water starts to doubt itself.
Then the small bright argument
of a minnow, and the whole grey sentence
resolves into a throat.

Fifty-three, in marketing for 25 years, and updating my resume for the first time in a decade. One bullet: "Rebuilt the email onboarding flow for a B2B SaaS product, A/B testing 14 variants; trial-to-paid conversion rose from 8.2% to 13.5%, adding $1.1M in ARR." Would love to hear what you make of it.

I own a flower shop and I'm training for my first marathon (week 10 of 16). Mon: rest. Tue: 8 miles easy. Wed: 6 miles with 3x1 mile at tempo. Thu: 5 easy plus strides, 20 min strength. Fri: rest. Sat: 16 mile long run, last 3 at goal pace. Sun: 4 recovery miles. Wedding season hits in May, so Fridays stay empty on purpose. What's your take?

My project: how does plate thickness affect Chladni patterns? I'll vibrate square aluminium plates (1, 1.5, 2 mm) with a speaker driver and sweep frequency until sand forms the same mode shape. Theory predicts frequency scales with thickness, so I'll plot f against t and see how close my data comes. I'll photograph each pattern. Does this seem like a good plan to you?

Here's the central question of my philosophy dissertation: "If moral testimony is epistemically legitimate in some domains, what explains why deferring to an expert about whether to donate seems acceptable while deferring about whether to forgive does not?" I'd appreciate your feedback.
I'm a linguist turned app founder. Our language-learning app's slogan is: "Be the one who orders for the table." Could you give me your thoughts on it?

Proud of this one from my SQL homework! Find students who've completed every required course:
SELECT s.name
FROM students s
JOIN enrollments e ON e.student_id = s.id AND e.completed
JOIN courses c ON c.id = e.course_id AND c.required
GROUP BY s.id, s.name
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT c.id) = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM courses WHERE required);
I'd really like your feedback on it.

I've been gardening for years and finally boiled the experience down: "My tomato plants and I have an understanding. I water them daily, and in return they produce eleven tomatoes, all on the same Tuesday, while I'm out of town." Does it read well to you?

I coach marathoners. My app is called Negative Split. Most pacing apps talk constantly, which drives me nuts. This one stays silent while you're within 5 seconds per mile of target. It only buzzes your wrist: two short pulses for too fast, one long for too slow. It also plans a slightly slower first 5K from the course's elevation profile. Can you give me feedback?

units: Pastry chef here, testing this for our autumn menu. Pear and rye tart: rye flour pâte sucrée, filled with brown butter frangipane (120g butter, browned and cooled; 120g almond flour; 100g sugar; 2 eggs). Fan thin slices of roasted Bosc pear on top, then glaze with thyme-infused honey and finish with flaky salt. Bake at 175°C for 38 minutes. I'd love an outside opinion before it goes on the menu.

My project compares 3D-printed infill patterns: gyroid, grid, and honeycomb. Each test cube is adjusted to exactly 12.0 g (±0.1) so strength is per unit mass. I print five of each and load them with sand until they fail, recording the mass of sand at the crack. Same filament, same print temperature. Tell me what you think, please. I'm happy to take criticism.

I'm 71 and my doctor mentioned osteopenia. Mon/Thu: 50 heel drops, step-ups in a 5 kg weighted vest, farmer carries with 8 kg. Tue/Sat: 45-minute brisk hill walk. Wed: tai chi class, plus one-minute single-leg stands while brushing my teeth. Fri: band rows, wall push-ups moving toward counter push-ups. Sun: gardening. I add 1 kg to the vest each month. I'd love to hear what you make of it.

I'm an urban planning student and I write a commuter blog. Title: "Mapping the Number 9 Bus." First sentence: "The 9 crosses eleven neighborhoods in forty minutes, which means that every morning I travel through three tax brackets, two languages, and one very opinionated pigeon." Okay, be honest: what's your reaction to this?

Drafting a grant request for a long-term beetle survey and trying a bolder opening: "We're asking you to fund the least glamorous work in conservation: counting. You cannot protect what you cannot number. Our twelve-year survey is the only reason we knew the wetland was failing years before the herons left. Counting is how we hear a warning while it's still a whisper." Does it work as a first paragraph for a funder?

I'm a nervous 12-year-old, but here goes. I noticed my dog's water bowl gets slimy faster outside than inside. I'm going to put 6 identical bowls out: 3 steel and 3 ceramic, half in shade and half in sun, and swab a 1 cm square from each bowl every day for 5 days. I'll then streak the swabs on agar and compare how many colonies grow. Please let me know what you think of the idea.

I'm in 6th grade and I'm testing paper airplane winglets. I made a launcher from a ruler and a rubber band pulled back to exactly 10 cm so every launch has the same speed. I'll fold 5 identical planes for each wing design (none, up, down, and split tips), throw each one 10 times, and record the glide distance from a fixed height. Then I'll calculate the glide ratio for each. Does this sound good to you?

Our running club coach Beth is retiring from teaching, and I volunteered to speak. Draft: "Beth's entire coaching philosophy was one sentence: 'You're not slow, you're early for the next mile.' I've repeated it on hills, in hospital corridors, once outside a divorce lawyer's office. Beth, you never timed us. You just stood at the finish line with a thermos, as if you'd always known we'd arrive." Honest thoughts welcome.

I'm 16 and run a mowing business with 14 customers. June plan: 14 × 4 visits × $35 = $1,960. Gas $86, trimmer line and blades $30, mower fund $150, flyers $20, tax set-aside 15% ($294), car savings $700, college $380, spending money $300. Zero left over. Mind giving me your honest opinion?

I'm a pediatric nurse and I wrote this for my patients. Opening: "The machine by Tomás's bed made three sounds. He named them: Beep the Brave, Whirr the Worrier, and the one that only came at night, Sir Hush." Over the book he makes friends with each. Could you tell me what you think? I'm a little nervous showing it to anyone.

Funnel conversion for our checkout flow, first timestamp per step so repeat visits don't inflate the counts:
WITH s AS (
  SELECT user_id,
    MIN(ts) FILTER (WHERE step = 'view') AS v,
    MIN(ts) FILTER (WHERE step = 'cart') AS c,
    MIN(ts) FILTER (WHERE step = 'pay') AS p
  FROM funnel_events GROUP BY user_id)
SELECT COUNT(v) AS viewed, COUNT(c) FILTER (WHERE c >= v) AS carted, COUNT(p) FILTER (WHERE p >= c AND c >= v) AS paid FROM s;
Casual question: how does it look?

The layout: a decomposed granite courtyard, a central ring of boulders around a palo verde for shade, agave and red yucca on the south edge, and a night-blooming cereus and white evening primrose along the patio. A drip line runs on one timer, three zones. Total water use is under 15% of our old lawn. What's your take?

I run a small bakery and I'm mentoring a student with this idea. Sourdough starter in identical clear jars, same flour and hydration, held at 18, 22, 26 and 30°C in water baths. Time-lapse photos mark rise height every 10 minutes. Then we compute peak-rise time and estimate Q10 for fermentation. Three jars per temperature. How would you rate the approach?

I'm studying literature and tried a folktale. "Tortoise Carries the News." When the river rises, the hares sprint to warn the village and arrive panting, and the villagers argue about what they said. Tortoise arrives hours later and says it once, calmly. Everyone's already packing, because he described every cracked bank he passed on the way. Does the ending earn its moral, in your view?

one wet second of me, passing.

and drop it behind me.
Somewhere past Kearney I say your name
to the windshield, which holds it a mile and lets go.

units:
My girlfriend and I are on opposite sides of the world for my exchange year, and I wrote this for her. Would you tell me how it reads to you?
You're eating breakfast in my tomorrow.
I'm finishing your yesterday's dinner.
We pass the same hour
like two people
on a very long staircase.

I roast coffee in my garage and I'm calling the brand Longitude. The logo is one coffee bean in dark espresso brown. The centre crease is a straight meridian line running top to bottom. A tiny dot sits on it, showing the exact spot of my town's coordinates, and the numbers are printed small underneath. Tell me what you think.
Hi! I'm 19 and just launched a tiny Etsy shop selling hand-knitted wool socks. My slogan: "Socks that make winter a rumour." Would love to hear what you think, even if it's blunt.

I'm a baker who codes on the side, and this turns recipe timings like "1h 30m" into milliseconds for my proofing timer. Thoughts?
```js
const units = { d: 864e5, h: 36e5, m: 6e4, s: 1e3 };
const toMs = str =>
  [...str.matchAll(/(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)\s*([dhms])/g)]
    .reduce((t, [, n, u]) => t + n * units[u], 0);
```

Retired court stenographer here, age 71. I've started on a screenplay, and this is my logline: "A 911 dispatcher takes a call from a woman who only whispers about her cat, and has eleven minutes to decode what the cat means before her abuser returns." I'd love an outside opinion, if you don't mind.

I'm a vet, and I want to start a dental plan for pets. $19 a month covers a yearly scaling under anesthesia, a home-brushing kit, and a video call with a tech every quarter to check your technique. I've seen too many dogs lose teeth at eight because the cleaning cost $600 at once. My plan makes that cost small and regular. Be honest, would you sign up your own dog?

I'm new to selling tea and a little nervous. Here's the description I wrote for one of my teas:
"Lapsang Souchong, smoked over pine. A campfire in a cold cabin: resinous, faintly sweet, with a surprising hint of dried longan on the finish. Steep at 95°C for three minutes. Try it with salty cheese, or with rain."
Could you tell me how it reads?

I'm putting this on my dog-grooming flyer: "Your dog can't tell you his ears hurt. He can only shake his head and look at you. A groomer sees mats, ticks, and lumps weeks before a vet appointment would. Book every six weeks and you get a clean dog and a second set of eyes." Does the tone feel right to you?

I'm 72 and my granddaughter doesn't speak Tagalog. So: in Lola's kitchen there's one rule, you can only ask for something by its name in the other language. "Pass the salt" becomes "asin," and soon Mari is hungry in two languages. Every page adds a word and a recipe. What's your opinion? Be honest, I've survived worse.

I'm a tailor, and my book is about trousers. "Hem" follows one pair of corduroys across three brothers. Each page the hem is let down an inch, and the pockets hold what the last boy left: a pebble, a bus ticket, a dried worm. On the final page the youngest hears the jingle and realizes he's wearing his brothers' whole childhoods. Tell me what you think!

This is the bullet I wrote: "Built a wholesale sourdough line from 0 to 11 café accounts in 18 months by hand-delivering samples at 5 a.m.; held waste under 4% with a par-level spreadsheet I designed." Thoughts?

I translate novels for a living, and I wrote a haiku about the part of the job that never makes it into interviews:
Last line of the book—
I leave one word as it was
like a light left on
How does it read to you? Any lines you'd question?

I run a tiny bakery and posted this on our Instagram story at 8:45 this morning: "Sold out of croissants by 8:40 again. To the man who asked if we'd make more: we would, but the butter has a schedule and so do I. Tomorrow's batch goes in at 5. Come at 7 and you'll have a croissant. Come at 9 and you'll have a story." Too cheeky? Let me know!

I wrote this for my little brother, whose dad works nights. "The House Is Wearing Its Quiet." Every afternoon Theo tiptoes through the rooms like they're a sleeping animal: cereal without crunching, cartoons on captions only. At four o'clock Dad's alarm rings, and the whole house exhales and gets loud again. How does it read to you? Be straight with me.

I'm 71 and my doctor mentioned osteopenia. Mon/Thu: 50 heel drops, step-ups in a 5 kg weighted vest, farmer carries with 8 kg. Tue/Sat: 45-minute brisk hill walk. Wed: tai chi class, plus one-minute single-leg stands while brushing my teeth. Fri: band rows, wall push-ups moving toward counter push-ups. Sun: gardening. I add 1 kg to the vest each month. I'd love to hear what you make of it.

I'm a college junior and I've been writing a coming-of-age novel about a boxing gym. Here's the first line: "The summer I turned sixteen I learned two things about my father's gym: that it smelled of liniment and forgiveness, and that nobody ever came there to win." Could you give me feedback?

Pitching my D&D group on the next campaign: "You're all accountants to the villains. Nobody swings a sword. Every fireball comes with an invoice, the dragon's hoard needs an audit, and the Dark Lord will be furious about Q3. Trust me, the most terrifying thing in any dungeon is a well-organized ledger." Would this get you to say yes, or should I tone down the absurdity?

I analyze my own online chess games for fun. Here's how I score my openings as Black, counting draws as half a point and ignoring openings I've played fewer than 20 times:
SELECT opening, COUNT(*) AS games,
  ROUND(AVG(CASE result WHEN 'win' THEN 1.0 WHEN 'draw' THEN 0.5 ELSE 0 END), 3) AS score
FROM games
WHERE color = 'black'
GROUP BY opening
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 20
ORDER BY score DESC;
What do you reckon?

```js
const emitter = () => {
  const subs = new Map();
  return {
    on(t, f) {
      (subs.get(t) ?? subs.set(t, new Set()).get(t)).add(f);
      return () => subs.get(t).delete(f);
    },
    emit(t, ...a) { subs.get(t)?.forEach(f => f(...a)); },
  };
};
```

  SELECT user_id,
    MIN(ts) FILTER (WHERE step = 'view') AS v,

    MIN(ts) FILTER (WHERE step = 'pay') AS p
  FROM funnel_events GROUP BY user_id)
SELECT COUNT(v) AS viewed, COUNT(c) FILTER (WHERE c >= v) AS carted, COUNT(p) FILTER (WHERE p >= c AND c >= v) AS paid FROM s;

Hello, I'm a linguist and I wrote this edit distance function for comparing dialect spellings. It only keeps one row in memory:
```python
def levenshtein(a, b):
    prev = range(len(b) + 1)
    for i, ca in enumerate(a, 1):
        cur = [i]
        for j, cb in enumerate(b, 1):
            cur.append(min(prev[j] + 1, cur[j-1] + 1, prev[j-1] + (ca != cb)))
        prev = cur
    return prev[-1]
```

```python
def levenshtein(a, b):
```

units: I'm a night-shift nurse, eleven years in, and I've finally started writing. Here's a title and opening line for my first post: "What the Night Shift Knows About Silence." "At 3:40 a.m. the hospital hums in B-flat, and after eleven years I can tell from a change in that hum which floor is about to have a bad hour." I'd really appreciate your feedback.

I'm a baker, so I'm up at 4am anyway. My cafe opens at 6:30 for the people on early shifts: bus drivers, midwives, cleaners. It's called "Half Past." You'd say, "Meet me at half past," and everybody knows it's an easy hour to get to. Just wondering what comes to mind when you read the name.

Written during a nap I did not get to finish. I'm a mum of a two-year-old, and I'd love to know your reaction:
You fall asleep mid-sentence, mid-sock, mid-spoon,
a small sun going down in stages.
I carry you the way you'd carry soup,
all of me arranged around not spilling.

I'm a PhD student and this is the first tweet of a thread I'm about to post: "Tardigrades survive the vacuum of space. Mine did not survive a long weekend in our lab cabinet. A thread on how they actually do it (a protein called Dsup shields their DNA) and why 'indestructible' is the wrong word. 1/" Should I change anything before I hit send?

I'm 68 and retired, and my main goal is staying steady on my feet for gardening and grandkids. Mon: 20 min walk, sit-to-stand 3x10, heel-to-toe walking. Tue: resistance bands, upper body. Wed: tai chi class. Thu: walk plus single-leg stands near the counter. Fri: light dumbbell work. Sat: garden (counts!). Sun: rest. Does this seem like a reasonable week to you?

I'm 71 and I sell jam at farmers' markets under my family name, Marlow's. For the logo I scanned the M from my late mother's recipe card, her actual handwriting, and traced it cleanly. Where the dot of ink had pooled at the end of the last stroke, I replaced it with a small thumbprint in jam red. Everything else is plain. I'd welcome your opinion.

I'm a geologist, and I wrote a book for my niece. "Every stone on the beach was waiting to become something. Dot only wanted to be thrown once, and touch the water seven times." She is, and she does, and then she sinks, slowly, to where the sand is made. Last page: a new beach. Would you give me your honest reaction?

Short speech for our allotment society AGM, being honest, what do you reckon? "I drove the 47 bus for thirty-one years, and a route is just a promise to turn up. Allotments are the same. Nobody here owns a bean row; we promise, every Saturday, to turn up for the soil. So when Margaret's marrows win again, remember: the soil won. Margaret just showed up."

I'm opening a vet clinic called Tailwind. The mark is a dog's tail, side-on, drawn as three nested arcs of decreasing length, each stroke a bit thinner. They read as a wag, but they also read as wind lines. The clinic name sits to the right in lowercase, and the arcs are teal. I'd love a candid reaction before I send it to the printer.

I own a laundromat, and my customers inspired a song, so here's the chorus. English is my second language, so I'm curious how the words sound to you. What do you think?
Spin cycle, spin cycle, the whole block's laundry turning,
I learned my English at the folding tables here.
Every lonely sock, I keep in a box by the door.
Someone always comes back, if you wait a year.

units: I'm a history teacher and I'm presenting at a regional conference on the Great Fire of London. I open: "Thomas Farriner told the court he'd put out his oven before bed, and three and a half centuries later I'd like to take him at his word." What do you think of it?

Here's my plan: road salt versus roadside grass. I'll germinate 50 native grass seeds per dish in NaCl solutions of 0, 1, 2, and 4 g/L, four dishes each. I'll count germinated seeds daily for 14 days and graph the curves, not just the final percentage, so delays show up. I also measure radicle length on day 14. Honest feedback welcome, please!

I do woodworking as a hobby and have started writing haiku in my shop notebook. Here's one. I'd love your opinion!
Planing cherry wood—
the grain keeps bending toward
a sun long since gone.

I'm a divorce lawyer, and I write romance on the side under a pen name. Here's my opening line: "The custody agreement gave Dev the house and Priya the sourdough starter, and neither of them, in the end, knew how to keep the thing alive." How does it read to you?

Freelance illustrator, income swings a lot. I budget off my lowest month of the last year, $2,400: rent 900; food 320; health insurance 210; phone/internet 90; software 55; transit 60; personal 125; tax account 640. Anything above that gets split: 30% tax, 40% buffer until I hit three months, 30% to me. Thoughts? Be blunt.

Proud of this one from my SQL homework! Find students who've completed every required course:
SELECT s.name
FROM students s
JOIN enrollments e ON e.student_id = s.id AND e.completed
JOIN courses c ON c.id = e.course_id AND c.required
GROUP BY s.id, s.name
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT c.id) = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM courses WHERE required);
I'd really like your feedback on it.

I analyze my own online chess games for fun. Here's how I score my openings as Black, counting draws as half a point and ignoring openings I've played fewer than 20 times:
SELECT opening, COUNT(*) AS games,
  ROUND(AVG(CASE result WHEN 'win' THEN 1.0 WHEN 'draw' THEN 0.5 ELSE 0 END), 3) AS score
FROM games
WHERE color = 'black'
GROUP BY opening
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 20
ORDER BY score DESC;
What do you reckon?

Nursing student here, about to put this on my profile. Can you tell me what you think?
Good at: finding a vein first try, parallel parking, remembering your dog's name.
Working on: sourdough, leaving the group chat on read, believing me when I say "I'm fine."
Night rotations mean my weekends are Tuesdays. If you can be cheerful about dinner at 8 a.m., we'll get along.

Okay, birders, here's my idea. Lots of us can't describe a song in words, so the app lets you tap the rhythm on the screen and draw the pitch as a rising or falling line. It narrows species by pattern, then plays three candidate recordings to compare. It would also work offline in the field. I'd really like an opinion before I try to prototype it.

Here's my idea: erosion control. I build four 30° slopes in trays: bare soil, grass, mulch, and gravel. A watering can with 100 drilled holes simulates 20 minutes of steady rain from a fixed height. I collect the runoff and dry it to find the sediment mass, and I measure the total water volume too. Three replicates per cover. What do you think?

Ladle the boiling congee over a bowl of raw minced scallion, ginger and salt so the heat wilts them. Top with a soft egg, soy, white pepper and chili crisp. Is this a decent recipe? Be honest!

Change how it opens." I charge $18 per garment. I'm a little shy about putting this out there. Please tell me what you think.

units:
I'm 63 and trying to ease toward retirement. Here's what I plan to send my manager. What's your view?
"Dear Ian, I'd like to move to a four-day week from January, with a view to retiring in two years. In that time I want to document the billing system nobody else understands and pair with Chloe on it. Should I put in a formal request, or is this enough to start?"

Our daughter cried when the snow melted, so I wrote this on my lunch breaks. "Snowman, Stored." Odile hides her snowman in the chest freezer between the peas and Dad's fish, visiting daily with a scarf. By July he's the size of a grapefruit. In December she introduces him to the first snowfall like a returning relative. I'm a plumber, not an author. Thoughts?

I'm a hobby glassblower, and our studio is adding a tiny coffee window. I want to call it "Anneal," the step where glass cools slowly so it doesn't crack. The menu's tagline would be "Slow down. Don't shatter." Thoughts on it?

I'm a junior copywriter, and this is my first pitch to a real client, a family-owned hearing-aid clinic. My line: "Hear the kettle again. The rain. Your granddaughter's whisper." Nervous to show it. How does it come across?

I'm a potter and wrote this between kiln loads. Chip is a mug with a cracked lip who gets hidden when guests come. During a power cut, small hands choose him, because the chip fits a thumb exactly. The last line: "Perfect is for looking at. Chip is for holding." I'm unsure whether to keep that ending as written. What would you do with it?

I'm a marine engineer starting a sailboat rigging business, Bowline Marine. The mark is a rope tied in a bowline, drawn as one thick line in navy. The loop of the knot forms the bowl of a capital B, and the standing part runs down as its stem. The working end of the rope tucks behind, and you can follow the knot correctly. Does it hold up, in your view?

Proposal to my team to kill our "smart suggestions" feature. Key paragraph: "Suggestions are used by 3% of users and generate 31% of our support tickets. Every feature is a promise to maintain it forever. We aren't deleting a feature; we're refusing a lifelong loan with a 3% return. Cut it, and move those two engineers to search, which 90% of users touch daily." Sending it Monday. Any thoughts first?

Nervous about this one! I'm a history major applying for archive internships, and this is my lead bullet: "Transcribed and indexed 312 pages of 1890s ledgers at the county archive, uncovering a pattern of wage withholding at a local cannery that became the basis of my 40-page honors thesis." Could you tell me what you think?

Hi! For my landscape studio course I designed a 12x20 ft Tucson courtyard. One desert willow in the northwest corner shades the hot afternoon wall. A dry-wash path of granite fines curves through brittlebush, Parry's penstemon and a single blue agave. A rain chain empties into a sunken basin planted with sedges. Seating sits on the east side for cool mornings. No turf. I present Thursday, so what's your take?

units: I'm a college sophomore and baked these for my floor. Brown butter miso cookies: brown 170g butter, chill until solid. Cream with 100g dark brown sugar, 50g white sugar, 1 tbsp white miso. Add 1 egg plus 1 yolk, 1 tsp vanilla, 220g flour, ½ tsp baking soda, ½ tsp salt. Fold in 150g chopped 70% chocolate. Rest dough 36 hours, bake at 180°C for 11 minutes, flaky salt on top. Honest thoughts on the recipe?

I'm 81 and this is the first poem I've ever shown anyone. My granddaughter set up this chat for me. I'd be glad to hear what you think.
At eighty I price the stairs by breath:
the fourth one costs a nickel,
the ninth, a dime.
I reach the landing, solvent still,
and spend what's left on the window.

Posting the tagline and description for my command-line tool. Be honest with me.
"tidy: finds the files you forgot you downloaded. It scans a folder, groups duplicates and stale installers, and shows what it would delete before touching anything. Nothing is removed without a y. Single binary, no config, 2 MB."
What would you change?

I translate novels for a living, and I wrote a haiku about the part of the job that never makes it into interviews:
Last line of the book—
I leave one word as it was
like a light left on
How does it read to you? Any lines you'd question?

I'm a farmer, and I set aside 1 acre on the edge of my property for a wildlife pond and meadow. A 20m x 10m pond with a shallow shelf on the south side, and a deep area of 2.5m on the north. A wildflower meadow, mown only in September, surrounds it, with a hedgerow of hawthorn, blackthorn, and dog rose on the windward side. A log pile and a stone hibernaculum for amphibians sits at the east end. Do you have any feedback?

I fish as a hobby and I'm toasting my dad and his second wife. "Dad taught me that fishing isn't about catching things. It's about sitting in a boat with someone, saying nothing, and being fine with that. After Mom, he stopped fishing for a few years. Then he met Carol, and last summer I saw them in the boat at dawn, not saying a word, perfectly fine. Dad, I'm glad you found someone to sit quiet with. To Dad and Carol."

Paralegal here, trying to move into litigation support. I'd love a second pair of eyes on this bullet: "Built a privilege-log template and tagging protocol that cut document review for a 400,000-page antitrust production from an estimated 9 weeks to 5, with zero clawback requests." What's your take?

Just a casual one: I teach myself screenwriting on YouTube and wrote this logline. "In 1889, a widowed schoolteacher enters the Oklahoma Land Run on a borrowed mule, carrying her husband's ashes and a map she has just realized he forged." Thoughts? Anything you'd change?

I run a tiny café and I'm testing a new morning bun. Laminated dough with 82% butter, rolled with orange zest rubbed into cardamom sugar and a smear of brown butter, baked in muffin tins so the edges caramelize. Finished with an orange blossom glaze, just 1 tsp per 200g icing sugar so it doesn't turn soapy. Would you put this on your menu? Please be straight with me.

units: I'm 63, been farming all my life, never given a speech. Tomorrow at the co-op I'll say: "Each of us owns a combine that sits idle 340 days a year. That's eleven machines, eleven loans, eleven rusting evenings. Buy one together and we each keep our money and lose only our pride. And my father's pride never once made a payment." Would that move you if you were sitting in the room?

I'm a grad student, writing a short story about my grandmother. Sharing the first paragraph with some nerves: "The telegram came on a Tuesday, which my grandmother held against Tuesdays for the rest of her life. She forgave the postman, the war, and eventually God. But Tuesdays she kept, the way a dog keeps a bone, and so for sixty years, every week, we ate cold supper and did not answer the door." What do you think?

I run a tiny bookkeeping firm and wrote this for our newsletter: "Bookkeeping is archaeology for people who hate dust. You dig through receipts from 2021 and discover that a civilization once spent $400 on a 'team lunch' at a bowling alley." Does it work, or should I cut it?

First-year law student. I told my study group: "The 'reasonable person' is the only one in law school who's never late, never confused, and has always done the reading." Everyone groaned in a good way, I think. What do you make of it?

I'm a barber, and I'm rolling out "Quiet Chair" on Sunday mornings. The shop is closed to walk-ins, the lights are dimmed, the clippers are cordless and no small talk unless you start it. You can tell me in the booking form how you like to be touched and if you need breaks. It was designed with my autistic nephew. $5 more than a regular cut. Would you book it?

Hey! I run a bakery and wrote a story for the kids who come in on Saturdays. Gerald, a sourdough starter, sulks when he's fed late, and six-year-old Pia learns to read his bubbles like moods. On the last page she tells him she'll be late on Monday, and apologizes first. Any thoughts? I'm mostly curious how it would work read aloud.

Powerlifting hobbyist, meet is in 8 days. Mon: squat 3x2 at 85%, bench 3x3 at 80%. Tue: rest. Wed: deadlift 2x2 at 85%, easy accessory work. Thu: bench singles up to 90%, short walk. Fri: rest. Sat: openers only, 30 min mobility. Sun: travel, light food, sleep. Volume drops about 40% while intensity stays high. Would love a second pair of eyes on this taper.

I'm a lifelong birder, and I've designed an app called Quiet List. You record a bird call and it identifies the species and adds it to your life list with a timestamp. For threatened species it saves your location only as a 10 km square, and it never uploads the exact spot. That way nesting sites stay safe, and your data still helps researchers. How does it sound to you?

I'm 65 and just retired after 40 years as a high school band director. At my party I said: 'Forty years of teenagers, and I've heard every wrong note a human can play. I miss none of them. I miss all of them. Please don't clap on one and three. And if you must cry, do it in tempo.' Casually curious how that works on paper.

units: I run a pottery studio and I'm starting a scholarship fund for teens. The letter opens: "Clay doesn't care about your grades. It doesn't care who your parents are, or whether you've eaten today. It only cares whether you're paying attention. We'd like to offer fifteen teenagers a seat at the wheel, free, for a year." How does it read to you?

My grandmother actually ran a dry cleaner, which inspired this. "A Korean grandmother who has worked in a Brooklyn dry cleaner for thirty years is the only witness who can identify a killer, but she has spent those years pretending not to speak English." Does this work for you? I'd love to hear your opinion.

I spent twelve years as a paralegal and I'm opening a cafe across from the county courthouse. The name: "Grounds for Appeal." Lawyers and jurors will be my main customers. Does it work for you, or would you change anything?

Posted this on my Instagram story during finals and a few friends replied, but I want a stranger's view: "Finals tip from someone who cried in the library stacks yesterday: you're not behind, you're in the middle. The middle always feels like failure because you can't see either shore. Drink water. Text a friend. Write only the next paragraph."

I illustrate on commission from my home studio and I'm pitching a children's book publisher. Here's the paragraph from my letter, wondering what you think.
"I draw the sort of picture a child finds on the third reading: the mouse behind the curtain, the half-eaten pear under the bed, the cat who looks guilty in every scene. My sketchbooks are full of these small secrets, and I would like to hide them in your books."

Flattening JSON order items in Postgres. Our orders come from three vendors, so the key isn't always present:
SELECT o.id, item->>'sku' AS sku, (item->>'qty')::int AS qty
FROM orders o
CROSS JOIN LATERAL jsonb_array_elements(o.payload->'items') AS item
WHERE o.payload ? 'items';
Backend dev, 2 years of experience. I'd like your thoughts, especially on whether I'm missing something.

I'm a 1600-rated club chess player writing up a project for fun. My question: "For players rated 1400 to 1800 in 15+10 online games, do time-trouble blunders cost more rating points than opening errors, and does that balance shift after a player's first thirty games?" I'd use Lichess data. Would love any opinion you have!

Hey! I'm a freshman and this is my first haiku since middle school. Wrote it walking to class this morning. Any thoughts?
First snow on campus—
the whole quad forgets its paths
until we make them.

I'm 40 and a T10 paraplegic. I want to build strength without wrecking my shoulders. Mon: seated cable rows 4x10, face pulls 3x15, landmine press 3x8. Tue: handcycle intervals, 6x2 min hard/2 easy. Wed: rest. Thu: lat pulldowns 4x8, parallel-bar dips 3x6, rotator cuff band work. Fri: 30-minute steady handcycle. Sat: Pallof presses and core. Sun: rest. Pulling volume is double pushing on purpose. Thoughts?

I'm a chef, and I wrote my best friend's wedding toast as a recipe. Ending: "Method: take two people who argue about salt. Add twelve years, one kitchen fire, and a very patient dog. Do not rush. Season with forgiveness, daily, to taste. Serves everyone at this table, who will leave fuller than they came. Tom, Maria: may you never run out." Honest thoughts?

units: For my education course I wrote "Tuesday Is Late." Leo waits at the front door for Tuesday, because Mum said it was coming. Through the day the postman arrives, then rain, then Grandma with a bag of oranges. By dinner Leo decides Tuesday is made of all of them. I'm a bit worried about it being too quiet for a read-aloud. Can you give me your honest take?

Hi! I'm 16 and I made these for my family's New Year dinner and I'm kind of nervous about sharing. Black sesame shortbread: 200g butter, 90g powdered sugar, 250g flour, 40g toasted ground black sesame, 1 tbsp orange zest, ½ tsp salt. Chill the dough 1 hour, slice, then roll the edges in raw sesame seeds. Bake at 160°C for 22 minutes. Could you tell me what you think?

I'm a public health officer, and this is the question I'm proposing for our county study: "In rural counties with a single pharmacy, how does closure alter 90-day adherence to antihypertensives, and is the effect mediated by travel distance or by losing a relationship with a pharmacist?" Any thoughts?

Here's my hellstrip plan, 8x25 ft, Ontario zone 5, casual and just for fun. Three height bands. Front: prairie dropseed at 18 in spacing, so it reads tidy to neighbours. Middle: golden alexanders, then pale purple coneflower, then anise hyssop for a May to September bloom run. Back: New England aster and little bluestem for October colour. Seedheads stay up until March for the finches. What would you change, if anything?
I run a used bookshop and wanted something for our window. I wrote: "Every book here has already been somebody's favourite." Tell me what you think, please. Be as blunt as you like.

I drive the Route 9 bus and write poems on my breaks. This is from the last run of the night. What do you think?
Route 9, final run. The bus exhales.
Rows of seats keep the shapes of strangers,
a dent here, a warmth there,
and I drive the empty ghosts back to the depot
with my headlights on for them.

I've been struggling and finally wrote this to my manager. I'm nervous. Can you tell me how it reads?
"Hi Lena, I need to be upfront: I've been running on empty since the audit and my work is slipping. I'd like to take the five leave days I have left next week, then talk about moving the Q3 report to someone else. I'd rather tell you now than miss it."

I'm 55 and started saving late, so I'm catching up. Take-home $5,400: mortgage 1,450; groceries 500; utilities 280; car 350; health insurance 400; 401k catch-up 1,000; HSA 300; help with my son's college 500; fun 200; misc 420. Feeling a bit anxious about it. How does this look to you?

Weekend baker here. My loaf: 500g bread flour, 100g whole wheat, 20g toasted barley flour, with cold roasted barley tea replacing the water (80% hydration). 20% levain, four stretch-and-folds, overnight cold proof, baked covered at 245°C for 20 minutes, then uncovered for 22. Does the formula make sense to you? Any tweaks you'd suggest?

Hey! I run a bakery and wrote a story for the kids who come in on Saturdays. Gerald, a sourdough starter, sulks when he's fed late, and six-year-old Pia learns to read his bubbles like moods. On the last page she tells him she'll be late on Monday, and apologizes first. Any thoughts? I'm mostly curious how it would work read aloud.

Because I forget things, my budget is automated on payday (TA income $1,700). Rent $720 and utilities $55 autopay; $200 auto-savings; $60 'forgetful tax' fund for late fees and lost stuff; groceries $250; phone $35; transit $70; books $60; $200 weekly cash envelopes ($50 × 4) for fun; $50 buffer. What do you think of the system?

i'm in 8th grade and my teacher said to pick a problem at our school. my thesis is: "Our cafeteria throws away about forty pounds of untouched food daily, and the cause isn't picky eaters but a twenty-minute lunch period that ends before students finish, so lunch should be lengthened before any composting program is considered." what do you think?

I'm 11 and my idea for an app is called Pet Shift. My family has one dog and four people, and he keeps getting fed twice. You tap "Fed Biscuit" once. If someone else tries to tap it within two hours, the phone says "Dad already fed Biscuit 12 minutes ago." Then it shows a picture of Biscuit looking guilty. What do you think? My mom said to ask someone who knows apps.

I run a little hardware store and wrote a rhyming book. Here's how it opens:
"When the owner turns the sign and the keys click twice,
the hammers call to order and the washers roll dice;
the tape measures argue about who's most long,
and the level says, 'Friends, you are all slightly wrong.'"
What do you think? I'm curious whether the rhythm holds up when read aloud.

I'm a development associate at a food bank applying for a director role. This is the bullet I'm sharing in my cover letter too: "Secured $480K in first-time foundation grants by pitching 23 funders; raised donor retention from 38% to 54% by personally calling every donor who gave over $100." How does it land for you?

I'm in 6th grade and I'm testing paper airplane winglets. I made a launcher from a ruler and a rubber band pulled back to exactly 10 cm so every launch has the same speed. I'll fold 5 identical planes for each wing design (none, up, down, and split tips), throw each one 10 times, and record the glide distance from a fixed height. Then I'll calculate the glide ratio for each. Does this sound good to you?

Twenty years on trawlers and I've never shown anyone what I scribble between hauls. Here's one:
Gutting cod at dawn—
the gulls and I agree on
what is worth keeping
Honest thoughts welcome, I can take it.

I teach physics and I'm opening our astronomy society's autumn meeting with this. "Vega's light left in the year our newest member was born, so tonight, when you look up, you're seeing Vega as a toddler. Every observing night is time travel with bad coffee. Bring a flask, bring a child, and let's go meet the past together." Could you tell me what you make of it?

I'm a beekeeper with six hives, and I planned a 10m x 10m forage garden to support them from March to October. Early: crocus, willow, and hellebores. Spring: lungwort, borage, and fruit blossoms. Summer: lime tree, phacelia, and marjoram. Autumn: ivy, Sedum, and asters. Hives are in the southeast corner, facing away from the path, with a 2m hedge forcing bees to fly up. What do you think of it?

units: I taught fourth grade for 34 years and I'm applying to be a docent at the natural history museum. This is my paragraph: "Every September I handed my students a whale vertebra I'd bought at a yard sale and said nothing for a full minute. The questions they asked in that silence taught me more about teaching than any training did. I'd like to bring that minute of silence to your visitors." Could you tell me what you make of it?

I own a laundromat, and last month I added an espresso bar in the front corner. I'm calling the whole place "Delicates." The sign would be hand-painted, cold-water-wash-label style. Curious what you make of it!
I teach yoga in a small studio above a pharmacy. Here's the slogan I wrote for the door: "Come as you are. Leave a little taller." Could you tell me what you think of it?

I'm 68 and retired, and I'm sick of mosquito-repelling phone apps. For my grandson's fair, we'll build a two-chamber choice box with a screen divider, put in 20 fruit flies, and then play the app's tone on only one side. A blinded helper chooses the side with a coin flip. After 10 minutes we count the flies per side. Then we'll repeat it 30 times and run a binomial test. What's your opinion?

I'm a nursing student and wrote this for my evidence-based practice course. "Among night-shift med-surg nurses, does a protected 20-minute nap at 3 a.m. reduce medication-administration near-misses in the final three hours of the shift, compared with no scheduled break?" Could you give me your honest opinion? I'm a little nervous about it.

Hi! I play chess competitively as a hobby, and I'm toasting two fellow club members. Here goes: "In chess, we say the opening is theory, the middlegame is imagination, and the endgame is technique. Raj and Claire skipped the opening, played a wildly imaginative middlegame in the club parking lot, and now they're in an endgame where the only rule is that nobody resigns. May every draw be by agreement. To Raj and Claire." Thoughts?

Hey, this is from my intro DB class project (a book review site). I wanted the top 3 rated books in each category:
SELECT c.name AS category, t.title, t.rating
FROM categories c
CROSS JOIN LATERAL (
  SELECT b.title, b.rating FROM books b
  WHERE b.category_id = c.id
  ORDER BY b.rating DESC, b.title
  LIMIT 3) t
ORDER BY c.name, t.rating DESC;
Would love to hear what you think!

Forty thousand sisters and none of them asks why,
they carry out the winter and they carry in July.
I've been trying to learn how a thing so small
can work like it's the only one and still be one of all.

```js
const shuffled = arr => {
  const a = [...arr];
  for (let i = a.length; i > 1; i--) {
    const j = Math.floor(Math.random() * i);

  return a;
};
```

units: I'm a nurse doing my master's and I'm a bit nervous about this one. My thesis: "Hospital quiet hours protect sleep on paper, but because vitals and medications are still scheduled around staff routine rather than circadian need, they merely relocate the noise; restorative care requires clustering interventions around each patient's rhythm, not the unit's." Does it read clearly to you?

I'm a medical interpreter and need to update my resume. Here's the bullet I'm working with: "Interpreted live for 300+ oncology consults in Mandarin and Cantonese; led creation of an 85-term bilingual glossary now used by the hospital's entire language services department." Does it work for you?

Here's one I've been saving for my chess club's newsletter: "My chess rating is like my houseplants: technically alive, and no one is sure why." I'm pretty nervous about sharing it since some of those guys are brutal. How would you rate it?

I'm 16 and wrote this for a school project. A kid is scared of the dark, but the Dark is scared of kids: they're loud, sticky, and own flashlights. First line: "Under Jonah's bed, the Dark was practicing its brave face." They end up hiding in the same closet. Does it work? Be real with me lol.

I wrote this chorus for my nana after she passed in March. I'm a sophomore and have never shared a song before, so my hands are a little shaky. Does it work for you?
You measured flour in the hollow of your palm,
salt by the weather, sugar by your mood.
Now I'm guessing in your chipped blue bowl,
and the bread comes out almost you,
and almost is a kind of company, too.

I'm cataloguing my vinyl collection in Postgres with a tags array. Wanted live jazz albums but no Christmas ones:
CREATE INDEX albums_tags_gin ON albums USING gin (tags);
SELECT title, artist
FROM albums
WHERE tags @> ARRAY['jazz', 'live']
  AND NOT tags && ARRAY['christmas']
ORDER BY artist, title;
I'd love to know how this strikes you.

I own a tiny bookshop and I'm launching 'Flights.' For $12 you fill in a short taste form (it includes 'a book you gave up on, and why'), and I choose three books for you. Keep one, return two unmarked within 14 days, and your $12 comes back as store credit. Returned books go on a 'flown once' shelf at 40% off. Opinions welcome!

I'm a night-shift nurse and cook when I'm exhausted, so this is a one-pot dinner. Toast 2 tsp cumin seeds in olive oil, add onion, garlic, then 1½ cups red lentils and 6 cups water. Simmer 20 minutes. Stir in the chopped rind of half a preserved lemon, finish with lots of black pepper and a spoon of yogurt. Chili butter on top. Does this sound like something worth making again?

I run a small flower farm and I'm speaking to a florists' association. This is how I want to begin: "A rose on your table has usually travelled eight thousand miles to get there. Tonight I'd like to introduce you to the ones that haven't." Could you give me your honest reaction?

I roast coffee out of my garage and I'm calling the brand Second Crack. The logo is a single coffee bean, top-down, in matte black. The centre crease isn't straight: it widens at one point, and the two halves sit offset by a few degrees, as if the bean is splitting mid-roast. Nothing else, no text in the mark. What's your opinion?

units: I make kombucha to sell at the farmers' market, and I'm designing a project about its pH during fermentation. I'll brew five identical 1 L jars, and test pH with a calibrated meter every 12 hours for 14 days. I'll also record the temperature, and taste-test safely only after day 7. The graph should show when it crosses pH 3.5. What would you say about the design?

I'm an amateur astronomer, and my brother asked me for a toast. "When you look at a star, you're seeing light that left it long ago. Some of those stars are gone by the time you notice them. I think of that when I look at Hana and Theo, because what I see tonight, two people lit from inside, started years ago, in a lab hallway, over a broken coffee machine. Keep shining across the distance. To Hana and Theo." Does that read as natural?

I'm a locksmith with a small business, and my daughter talked me into blogging. Title: "Locked Out at 2 a.m.: A Locksmith's Field Guide to Humility." First sentence: "Nobody calls me because they're having a good night, so the first thing I do on every job is say something small and kind, because the door is the easy part." What do you make of it?
I'm a dog walker and I'm putting together business cards. The slogan I wrote is "Tired dogs, happy couches." Can you tell me what you think? I'm a bit nervous about showing it to anyone.

I'm a line cook who got curious about browning. I'll caramelize identical onion slices in solutions of baking soda at five different pH levels, then photograph each batch every 5 minutes next to a gray card and convert the pixels to L*a*b* color values. Then I'll plot how fast browning happens against pH. I'm a little nervous presenting at a science fair as a non-scientist. What do you think of it?

I'm a 29-year-old climber working toward my first 8a. Mon: 4 max hangs on a 20mm edge (10 s, +5 kg), then limit bouldering. Tue: 40-minute zone-2 bike, core. Wed: rest. Thu: 4x4s on routes two grades below my limit. Fri: push-ups, reverse wrist curls, shoulder external rotation. Sat: project attempts while fresh. Sun: rest. Every fourth week I halve the volume. How does it look to you?

Preserved lemon and olive chicken. Marinate thighs overnight in ras el hanout, grated onion, ginger and saffron steeped in warm water. Brown, then braise over low heat on a bed of onions with no added water for 45 minutes. Add the rind of one preserved lemon (pith removed) and green olives for the last 15 minutes. Finish with cilantro. Would you adjust anything?

I'm a retired schoolteacher and volunteer for our branch library. Here's how my fundraising letter opens: "Dear neighbor, In 1952 the Alder Street Library had 3,000 books and one stove. Today it has 11,000 books and the same stove. We are asking you to help us buy a new one, and, while we're at it, a roof." Any thoughts?

I'm a line cook turned kitchen manager, 31, working on my first startup. Pitch: "We give restaurants a free fryer-oil sensor that tells them the day the oil actually goes bad instead of the day the schedule says, and we take a cut of the oil they save." Does that come across clearly? Curious what you think.

I'm a stay-at-home dad and write a little blog for family and friends. Newest post: "My Son Narrates His Own Life and I Am Taking Notes." First line: "At four, Theo describes every action in the third person, 'Theo is putting on the sock, the sock is reluctant,' and I have started to suspect he's the only one of us paying attention." What do you make of it?

units: Music theory student here, and I'm opening my class presentation at the piano: "Play any two notes a half-step apart and you'll feel uneasy. That unease is why the shark in Jaws works, and I'm going to show you how to make it with two fingers." Would love to hear what you think.

I run a food truck (Korean-Mexican, mostly kimchi quesadillas) and wrote my profile in the same spirit. How's it land?
"I feed strangers from a window for twelve hours a day, so I'm excellent at small talk and terrible at days off. Looking for someone to sit on my truck's tailgate at midnight and tell me what I should put on the specials board. I'll pay in quesadillas. Vegetarian options available. I'm not heartless."

I'm the groom's boss, and I was asked to speak, which I assume means they ran out of friends. My line: "In six years Hugo has never missed a deadline except one: the Friday he left early to propose. I've never been so glad to be let down. Tess, we got a great employee. You got the rest of him, and I'm told that's the better deal." Thoughts?

I fish as a hobby and I'm toasting my dad and his second wife. "Dad taught me that fishing isn't about catching things. It's about sitting in a boat with someone, saying nothing, and being fine with that. After Mom, he stopped fishing for a few years. Then he met Carol, and last summer I saw them in the boat at dawn, not saying a word, perfectly fine. Dad, I'm glad you found someone to sit quiet with. To Dad and Carol."

I'm 24 and I've been a barista since I was 18. My pitch: "One loyalty card that works at every independent cafe in a neighborhood, funded by a 1% fee, so locals get their free tenth coffee and the chains' apps lose their advantage." Any thoughts? I haven't shown it to anyone yet.

I'm the mayor of a town of 6,000 and I'm campaigning for the library levy. Here's a section of my speech: "A library is the last place in town where you can walk in with no money and nobody asks why you're there. It costs the average household $41 a year. Ask yourself what else you can buy that's open to everyone, including the person you'd never think of." How does that sit with you?

Hi! I'm a pastry chef and I've been writing posts for my bakery's site. New one is called "Why Your Croissants Taste Like Bread With Ambitions." It opens: "Butter doesn't melt at 32°C so much as give up, and the exact moment it does is the whole reason your lamination collapses." Thoughts?

I coach a running club and I'm writing my first screenplay. Logline: "A blind marathoner's guide runner begins to lose his own sight, and neither man tells the other." I'm a bit nervous putting it out there. What's your take?

I'm a farmer, new to writing. In the town of Marl, your umbrella opens onto whatever you're feeling: Grandpa's makes drizzle, the mayor's makes hail. Nell's opens only sunshine, because she never lets anyone see her sad. The day it finally drizzles over her, the whole town comes to stand underneath. Tell me what you think, please.

I wrote this for my little brother, whose dad works nights. "The House Is Wearing Its Quiet." Every afternoon Theo tiptoes through the rooms like they're a sleeping animal: cereal without crunching, cartoons on captions only. At four o'clock Dad's alarm rings, and the whole house exhales and gets loud again. How does it read to you? Be straight with me.

units:
I run a little hardware store and wrote a rhyming book. Here's how it opens:
"When the owner turns the sign and the keys click twice,
the hammers call to order and the washers roll dice;
the tape measures argue about who's most long,
and the level says, 'Friends, you are all slightly wrong.'"
What do you think? I'm curious whether the rhythm holds up when read aloud.

Pastry chef here, testing this for our autumn menu. Pear and rye tart: rye flour pâte sucrée, filled with brown butter frangipane (120g butter, browned and cooled; 120g almond flour; 100g sugar; 2 eggs). Fan thin slices of roasted Bosc pear on top, then glaze with thyme-infused honey and finish with flaky salt. Bake at 175°C for 38 minutes. I'd love an outside opinion before it goes on the menu.

Photography is my hobby, and I'm selling prints for the first time. Here's my listing text: "Fog at Pigeon Point, 12x18 archival pigment print on cotton rag paper. Shot at 5:40 a.m., it holds seven shades of grey between the lighthouse and the sea. Signed, numbered, edition of 50. Ships flat in a rigid mailer, with a card telling you where I stood." Feedback welcome.

Birding hobbyist here. I put this on Facebook yesterday: "5:42am, Marsden Reedbed. The bittern stood so still I spent ten minutes admiring a reed. Then the reed blinked. Lifer #212, and I forgot to breathe for most of it." Curious how it reads to someone outside the birding world?

This is the new homepage copy for my plumbing company: "A $20 valve inspection is boring. A flooded kitchen at 2 a.m. is not. Most of our emergency calls started as a drip someone meant to look at. Book a yearly check, and the only exciting thing in your house will be dinner." Does it sound like a real person wrote it?

Student cooking for my flatmates. My cacio e pepe variation: toast black pepper and 1 tsp red Sichuan peppercorns, crush coarsely. Cook 100g tonnarelli in very little water so the starch stays high, and pull it 2 minutes early. Off the heat, mix Pecorino with pasta water into a paste first, then toss everything together with the pepper. Can you give me feedback on the technique?

I'm a chef, and I wrote my best friend's wedding toast as a recipe. Ending: "Method: take two people who argue about salt. Add twelve years, one kitchen fire, and a very patient dog. Do not rush. Season with forgiveness, daily, to taste. Serves everyone at this table, who will leave fuller than they came. Tom, Maria: may you never run out." Honest thoughts?

I'm a barista, 27, applying to a coffee roaster's quality control team. Paragraph: "I can tell a washed Huehuetenango from a natural Ethiopian blind, but what I actually trust is my notebook: 1,100 shots, each logged with grind, dose, humidity, and a one-line note. Taste fades by lunchtime. Records don't. I'd like to be the person who writes down what the rest of us forget." Thoughts?

My little cousin stutters, and I wrote this for him. Caleb notices the river stutters too, tripping over every rock ("b-b-bubble, b-b-bubble"), yet it reaches the sea every single time. Nobody in the book ever says "fix." He just sits beside the water and talks back to it. I'm a bit nervous about getting it right. Would you mind giving me honest feedback?
