units: I run a little pottery studio and want to stop guessing about cracking. Here's what I wrote in my notebook: "Does adding 5% grog by weight to our stoneware body reduce cracking in pieces thicker than 2 cm during bisque firing at a ramp of 100°C per hour?" I'd fire matched test tiles. Does this seem like a good question to you?

This is the sign I taped to my plant shop door and then photographed for Instagram: "Closed Monday for my daughter's piano recital. She's playing Clair de Lune and has warned me that if I cry, she'll know. The ferns are holding the fort. Back Tuesday, 9am." Any feedback?

I'm a theater major applying for stage management internships. Here's the bullet for my last show: "Stage-managed a 24-person production of Our Town on a $900 budget; built and called a 140-cue lighting and sound script across 12 performances with zero missed cues." What do you think?

I keep bees, and I sell honey at the farmers' market, so I mapped a forage plan for my 1-acre lot. A six-foot hedge of serviceberry and pussy willow sits in front of the hives to force a high flight path. Bloom runs in order: willow in March, crocus, then lilac, then basswood, then borage and buckwheat in July. Asters and goldenrod go in for autumn. A shallow water dish with pebbles sits 10 ft from the hives. Does it look sensible?

I'm a software engineer and I've planned a 5m x 7m garden inspired by Japanese design, but adapted to Ohio. The idea: three clustered stones in an area of raked gravel, shaped like a dry stream. It's crossed by a flat stone bridge. A Japanese maple stands in the corner, and I've placed moss under a shaded eave. I'm keeping the plant list to nine species, and nothing is symmetrical. Here's the plan. What do you think?

I'm a civil engineering technician and I'm planning a mini concrete project for my niece. We'll cast 12 beams (4x4x16 cm) with 0, 1%, 2%, and 3% fibers by volume (hair, straw, or shredded plastic bags). Each beam is supported at both ends, and a bucket on the middle slowly fills with sand until the beam breaks. The failure load is divided by the beam's mass. All beams will cure 28 days. Does this seem like a solid project?

I'm a weekend woodworker selling at a craft fair, and this is my sign copy. "End-grain walnut and maple board, 14 x 10 inches. Knife edges sink between the fibers and the grain closes behind them, so your blades stay sharper and the board shows fewer scars. Finished with mineral oil and beeswax. About six pounds, heavy enough to stay put while you chop." Any thoughts?

I run a one-item dumpling food truck and I'm pitching to a festival committee next week. Here's how I'm starting: "My truck sells exactly one thing, a dumpling, and in the next ten minutes I'm going to convince you that's a strategy and not a limitation." Can you tell me your opinion?

Mom of three, so my workouts ride on existing routines. Mon: while the pasta boils, 3 rounds of 10 squats and 10 counter push-ups. Tue: school-run walk, pushing the stroller up the big hill. Wed: during swim lessons, 30 laps. Thu: 20-minute kettlebell video while the kids watch a show. Fri: 15-minute kitchen dance party. Sat: family hike carrying the youngest. Sun: rest. Does this seem sustainable?

made a card game w my friends and wrote the back-of-box blurb
"Heist Night. 3–6 players. You're a crew of thieves robbing a museum, and one of you is secretly the informant. Play cards to crack the vault, or quietly sabotage it. 20 minutes, no board, one very suspicious silence. Trust is a resource. Spend wisely."
what do u think??

units: I'm a farmer, and I set aside 1 acre on the edge of my property for a wildlife pond and meadow. A 20m x 10m pond with a shallow shelf on the south side, and a deep area of 2.5m on the north. A wildflower meadow, mown only in September, surrounds it, with a hedgerow of hawthorn, blackthorn, and dog rose on the windward side. A log pile and a stone hibernaculum for amphibians sits at the east end. Do you have any feedback?

Hi! I'm a line cook, six years in, applying for a sous chef job. Here's the middle paragraph of my letter: "At Marlow's I cut our walk-in waste from 14% to 5% by turning trim into the staff meal, then the staff meal into a Thursday special that outsold the ribeye. I'm not interested in cooking expensive food. I'm interested in making sure nothing that enters your kitchen dies in the bin." Honest thoughts?
I'm a dog walker and I'm putting together business cards. The slogan I wrote is "Tired dogs, happy couches." Can you tell me what you think? I'm a bit nervous about showing it to anyone.

My project compares 3D-printed infill patterns: gyroid, grid, and honeycomb. Each test cube is adjusted to exactly 12.0 g (±0.1) so strength is per unit mass. I print five of each and load them with sand until they fail, recording the mass of sand at the crack. Same filament, same print temperature. Tell me what you think, please. I'm happy to take criticism.

I run a bike repair shop and I'm finally writing for our website. Title: "Your Bike Isn't Making That Noise to Annoy You." Opening: "Every click, tick, and groan from a bicycle is a tiny confession, and after eleven years of fixing them above a laundromat, I can usually tell you what yours did last weekend before you finish describing the sound." Feedback welcome!
I'm a linguist turned app founder. Our language-learning app's slogan is: "Be the one who orders for the table." Could you give me your thoughts on it?

I'm a school librarian and an immigrant, and I wrote this one for me too. Linh collects the wrong ways people say her name in jars: Lin, Lynn, Lean. Her grandmother says each jar is a small gift from someone who tried. On the last page, a new teacher asks Linh to say it first. I'd love your thoughts, truly.

I've played jazz piano for thirty years but only recently started writing my own lyrics. Here's a ballad chorus:
The moon is a borrowed coat tonight
Too wide in the shoulders, it still smells of you
I wear it down the avenue
Pretending that it's mine, pretending that it's new
I'd value your impressions.

I've been a newspaper copy editor for thirty years and I'm trying screenwriting. Logline: "Two obituary writers at a dying small-town paper, long at war over each other's prose, each begin secretly writing the other's obituary, the most honest work either has done in years." What do you make of it?

I've been a landlord for 15 years, and I've seen too many deposit fights. My app idea is Day One. At move-in, tenant and landlord walk through together. The app guides them room by room, with a required photo of each wall, floor and appliance. Each photo is timestamped and cryptographically hashed. At the end, both sign and get the same PDF. Would tenants actually use this? What do you think?

units: I run a bike repair shop and I'm finally writing for our website. Title: "Your Bike Isn't Making That Noise to Annoy You." Opening: "Every click, tick, and groan from a bicycle is a tiny confession, and after eleven years of fixing them above a laundromat, I can usually tell you what yours did last weekend before you finish describing the sound." Feedback welcome!

I keep bees, and I hate pulling off my gloves to take notes. My app is Hive Voice. During an inspection I say "Hive 4, queen seen, eggs yes, six frames of brood, a little crowded," and it fills in a structured log. It flags anything missing, like "No mention of mites." It also compares the entry with last month's. Is this something you could see helping people?

Hobbyist beekeeper here. Our club's oldest member, Arlo, is hanging up his veil. My toast: "Arlo told me bees don't care about your day. Move slow, breathe, and they'll let you in. I've tried to live that way since. Sixty years, millions of bees, and only eleven stings, he claims. Arlo, you kept the hives and the humans calm. We'll leave the smoker lit for you." Do you think it works?

I'm a night-shift nurse and cook when I'm exhausted, so this is a one-pot dinner. Toast 2 tsp cumin seeds in olive oil, add onion, garlic, then 1½ cups red lentils and 6 cups water. Simmer 20 minutes. Stir in the chopped rind of half a preserved lemon, finish with lots of black pepper and a spoon of yogurt. Chili butter on top. Does this sound like something worth making again?

Hey, I coach distance runners and write a small newsletter. Next post is titled "Mile 20 Is a Negotiation." I open with: "Nobody warns you that at mile twenty your body will open with a lowball offer, and the whole skill of the sport is knowing it's only the first one." Could you tell me how this reads to you?

I'm a backend developer applying to a food bank's tech team, taking a pay cut to do it. Cover letter paragraph: "Last year I rewrote our checkout retry logic and saved my company an estimated $2M. This year I'd like to spend my skills on a problem where success is a Tuesday pantry line that moves twelve minutes faster. Your volunteer scheduler has a race condition. I found it in ten minutes and would love to fix it." How does it land?

Here's a Threads post I wrote about a film I love, would love your take: "Spirited Away is the only movie I know where the scariest scene is a man being kind to you. No-Face's loneliness works because nobody in the bathhouse ever asks what he actually wants."

Our knitting group has two speeds: "I'll finish it by Christmas" and "Which Christmas?" I said that at last week's meetup and got a laugh, but I'm wondering whether it holds up written down. What do you think, any tweaks?

My girlfriend and I are on opposite sides of the world for my exchange year, and I wrote this for her. Would you tell me how it reads to you?
You're eating breakfast in my tomorrow.
I'm finishing your yesterday's dinner.
We pass the same hour
like two people
on a very long staircase.

I own a small print shop and needed delivery dates that skip weekends and holidays. This is what I came up with. Thoughts?
```python
from datetime import timedelta
def add_business_days(start, n, holidays=frozenset()):
    step = 1 if n >= 0 else -1
    d = start
    while n:
        d += timedelta(days=step)
        if d.weekday() < 5 and d not in holidays:
            n -= step
    return d
```

units: I'm a bike mechanic, and I want to open a repair cart outside the train station. You drop your bike at 8 a.m. with a tag that lists the issues, and I text you a quote before 9. If you reply "yes," it's done by 5:30, and you pick it up on your way home. If you reply "no," it's free of charge to wait. No shop rent, just a cart and a trailer. What do you think about this idea?

I'm 16, a goalkeeper, and season starts in six weeks. Mon: box jumps 4x4, band-resisted lateral shuffles. Tue: team practice. Wed: pull-ups 4x6, Nordic curls 3x5, Copenhagen planks. Thu: practice, then 10 minutes of tennis-ball reaction catches off a wall. Fri: mobility only. Sat: match. Sun: easy swim, shoulder prehab. Nothing heavy within 48 hours of a match, so I planned around that. Any thoughts? Be straight with me.

I've kept a sourdough starter for four years and decided to write about it. Thesis: "Pandemic sourdough was less a food trend than a time trend: a starter demands feeding on a schedule, and people locked at home wanted something that made the days measurably pass." Any reactions?

I've been running tabletop RPG campaigns for friends for years and I'm trying to break into game design. Here's my resume bullet: "Designed and ran a 3-year campaign for 7 players; rewrote the combat system after playtests showed fights averaging 94 minutes, cutting them to 35 while preserving player choice." Any feedback?

Nervous about sharing this, but here's the thesis for my game design class essay: "Tetris endures not because it is simple but because it is unwinnable: its design turns inevitable failure into a measure of skill, teaching players to take pleasure in managing loss rather than avoiding it." Would love your reaction.

I'm a high school junior and wrote this for a film club pitch night. "When a stroke leaves her grandfather speaking only the Cantonese he spent fifty years hiding, a sixteen-year-old who never learned it has one summer to decode his confession." How would you react to this as a pitch?

```python
        row = [a + b for a, b in zip([0] + row, row + [0])]
```

What do you make of it?

I press my ear to the wood
and hear them, still there

units: I've been given the lease on a lighthouse keeper's cottage on the Northumberland coast, and I'm turning it into a cafe. The name is "Last Light." We'll close at dusk, so you can watch the lamp come on while you finish your tea. I'm 62 and a bit sentimental about it. What's your reaction to the name?

I supervise a warehouse and I'm not much of a writer. This is going to my manager. Any thoughts?
"Karen, Bay 4's forklift aisle is 2.1m wide; the new pallets need 2.4. Two near-misses this month, photos attached. Options: move the racking (about a day, no cost) or make the aisle one-way. I'd move the racking; I can do it Saturday with two people. Need your OK by Thursday."

I'm a 911 dispatcher, 48. Here's what I said at Carla's last-shift party: 'Carla has been the first voice on the worst day of ten thousand lives. She never got to see how any of them ended. She just said, "Stay on the line with me," and they did. Tonight, Carla, we're the ones saying it. Stay on the line. Visit. Bring the good cookies.' Nervous to share. Thoughts?

Long-time fantasy reader, first-time writer here. My novel begins: "Tuesday was the day Thornwick hid its children, so the dragon's tax collector found only goats, a very old man, and an unusually loud silence." Would you tell me what you think? Be gentle, I'm a bit anxious about this.

I'm a student and wrote a short poem for my Instagram, kind of nervous to ask but what do you think? "My grandmother counts in two languages: / Polish for coins and stairs, / English for the days since Dziadek, / and for the rosary, no language, / only the click of the next bead."

I teach bike repair as a hobby and want to run a workshop at the shop where I work. Pitching my manager:
"Hi Gus, what about a free 'Fix Your Own Flat' class, Saturdays at 10, six people max? We'd supply two spare tubes each, which cost us about $4, and attendees tend to buy levers and patch kits afterward. I'd teach it on my own time. Can we try one in April? Thanks, Wren"
What do you think?

Bootcamp student here. I needed to turn nested config into flat keys and ended up with this recursive version. How would you rate it?
```js
const flat = (o, p = '') =>
  Object.entries(o).flatMap(([k, v]) =>
    v && typeof v === 'object' ? flat(v, p + k + '.') : [[p + k, v]]);
Object.fromEntries(flat({ a: { b: 1, c: { d: 2 } } }));
```

Tonight I'm opening our astronomy club's star party. Here's the speech: "The light you'll see in Andromeda left 2.5 million years ago, before anything we'd call human. It has been traveling toward this field, this telescope, this paper cup of cocoa in your hand. Please don't rush. It's waited a long time for you. Red flashlights only, and be kind to the dark." What do you reckon?

I'm into amateur radio, and this is my idea. Two ESP32 LoRa boards log signal strength (RSSI) at 25 m intervals through dense forest and across an open field of the same length. I'll fit a path-loss model to both and compare the exponents. I'll repeat in summer and after leaf drop. I'm kind of proud of this one. What's your take?

I'm a hobbyist drone photographer and want to pitch a hotel manager. Here's the email:
"Dear Ms. Aoki, I'm a local photographer, and last week at golden hour I shot your hotel's rooftop terrace from above, attached. The frame shows the pool, the hills behind, and the sunset hitting the cabanas. I'd be glad to shoot a full set of ten images for your website for $250. I'm licensed to fly in this area. May I send a quote? Regards, Daniel"
What do you think?

units: I'm a bassist who's been touring for ten years and this has happened to me twice. "When a band's player gets sick the night before a gig, we get a vetted session musician who has already studied their charts and setlist into the van within twelve hours." What do you think?

I'm a retired machinist and now I do science fairs with kids. This year's project: does a pendulum's period change with amplitude as much as the equation says? We'll film a 1 m pendulum at 5°, 15°, 30°, 45°, and 60° with a 240 fps phone camera, extract the period frame by frame, and compare it to the small-angle formula and the elliptic-integral correction. We'd like to know how this comes across.

Pareto analysis for our catalogue: what share of revenue the top products make. I added the tie-breaker and ROWS frame deliberately.
WITH r AS (SELECT product_id, SUM(revenue) AS rev FROM sales GROUP BY product_id)
SELECT product_id, rev,
  SUM(rev) OVER (ORDER BY rev DESC, product_id ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) / SUM(rev) OVER () AS cum_share
FROM r ORDER BY rev DESC, product_id;
I'm a finance manager, not a developer. Does this look right to you?

My grandmother takes seven pills a day and gets confused about which she's had. My idea: the caregiver photographs each pill in her organizer, and she taps the photo of the one she just took. No reading required. The family gets one quiet summary each evening, not constant alerts. I'd like to know what you think before I show it to my aunts.

I'm a hobbyist game designer. Memory-care homes seem to run on bingo, so I made a kit: large tiles with photos of 1950s kitchen objects that residents match and talk about, plus a facilitator card with three open questions. $65 per kit. One activity director tried it, and residents were still chatting after 40 minutes. I'd like to sell it to care homes. What's your take?

I'm a line cook who got curious about browning. I'll caramelize identical onion slices in solutions of baking soda at five different pH levels, then photograph each batch every 5 minutes next to a gray card and convert the pixels to L*a*b* color values. Then I'll plot how fast browning happens against pH. I'm a little nervous presenting at a science fair as a non-scientist. What do you think of it?

```js
const memoize = fn => {
  const cache = new Map();
  return (...args) => {
    const key = JSON.stringify(args);
    if (!cache.has(key)) cache.set(key, fn(...args));
    return cache.get(key);
  };
};
```

units: Here's a Threads post I wrote about a film I love, would love your take: "Spirited Away is the only movie I know where the scariest scene is a man being kind to you. No-Face's loneliness works because nobody in the bathhouse ever asks what he actually wants."

Flight instructor here, applying to a regional airline. This is the bullet I lead with: "Instructed 47 students to private pilot certificates with a 94% first-attempt checkride pass rate, versus a 71% national average." Curious how it reads to someone outside aviation. Thoughts?

I run a little toy shop and wrote a fable for the kids who come in on Saturdays. Here's how it begins. Would you tell me what you think? "Once there was a clock that was always seven minutes slow, and the town loved it for exactly that reason. Late for church? Blame the clock. Late for love? The clock. It carried the town's small sins like a mule, until the day a clockmaker arrived, tool bag in hand, offering to help."

I own a little flower shop and wrote this on my lunch break. Showing it to you first, before anyone I know:
I can tell which bouquets will be forgiven
by how the man holds them:
like a question,
or like an alibi.
How does it read to you?

Retired DBA here, tinkering for fun. I wrote an org chart query for our club's volunteer table. Cycle guard included, since people enter data badly:
WITH RECURSIVE chain AS (
  SELECT id, name, manager_id, name::text AS path, 0 AS depth FROM staff WHERE manager_id IS NULL
  UNION ALL
  SELECT e.id, e.name, e.manager_id, c.path || ' > ' || e.name, c.depth + 1
  FROM staff e JOIN chain c ON e.manager_id = c.id WHERE c.depth < 12)
SELECT * FROM chain ORDER BY path;
What's your opinion?

I'm 14 and I like music, so I'm doing Chladni plates. I'm bolting a 20 cm square aluminum plate to a speaker driver, sprinkling salt on it, and sweeping frequencies from 100 to 3000 Hz. I'll photograph each pattern at resonance, then compare the frequencies to the theoretical plate-mode formula to find which ones match. I'll also test how the patterns change when I clamp the plate at its center vs. its edge. What do you think?

I run a used bookshop and wrote a jazzy little number about it. Here's the chorus. I'd be curious about your reaction, whatever it is.
Every book on this shelf was somebody's Tuesday night,
a train ride, a bathtub, a borrowed flashlight.
I just keep the kettle on and the lamp lit low,
and the dead keep writing to whoever's up.

Software engineer by day, haiku hobbyist by night. This one came from a late release:
Deploy at midnight—
rain on the office window
writes its own log lines
Curious how it reads to a non-programmer. Thoughts?

This is my first draft for an industrial design class assignment. "Halo Clip is a rear bike light that wraps around the seatpost and glows in a full ring, so drivers see you from the side as well as behind. USB-C charging, 12-hour runtime, and a silicone band that fits any post from 25 to 35 mm. At 41 grams, it weighs less than two AA batteries." Thoughts?

I'm a mechanic, 52, and my daughter says I should show somebody this. So here goes. Tell me what you think.
Under the hood the engine's cooled to a tick,
a metal clock winding down its day.
I wipe my hands on a rag that's been
every color of every car I've loved.

"Hi Dana, I have organic chemistry finals May 6 and 9, so I can't do my Thursday closes those weeks. Priya and Marcus both said they'd take them if I cover their Sunday opens on the 12th and 19th. I've already put the swaps in the shared sheet. If anything clashes, I'm happy to rework it. Thanks, Leo"
What do you think?

Sorry if this is a bit odd. I work in a post office sorting room and this came to me on shift. The start of my story:
"The dead letter office in Perth received, in 1962, a parcel containing forty-one left shoes. No note, no sender. Winifred Ames, who had spent nineteen years reuniting strangers with their mistakes, laid them in a row on the sorting table and felt, for the first time, outmatched."
What's your take?

I'm nineteen and writing a dystopian novel for NaNoWriMo. It starts like this: "In the Ministry of Weather, I was the only person who knew it hadn't rained by itself in thirty years." Does it hook you? I'd really like an outside opinion.

I'm opening a chess café named En Passant. The logo is a pawn in solid black, front-on. But its round head is a coffee cup seen from above: a ring, dark liquid inside, and a small handle at the right side where a pawn would have nothing. Everything else is perfectly standard. I'd like your opinion, please.

I own a small bakery and I'm writing a post to explain our prices. Title: "Why Our Croissants Cost $4.50." First sentence: "A croissant is three days of waiting disguised as breakfast: one day for the dough, one for the butter to settle into it, and one for me to stop touching it." Could you tell me your impressions?

I teach seventh grade and wrote this on the staffroom whiteboard today: "Teaching teenagers is like being a human Wi-Fi router: everyone's staring at me, nobody's connected, and the moment I move, they complain about the signal." Curious what people outside teaching make of it.

I'm a chess club coach opening a quick takeaway cafe next to the park tables where people play. I'd like to name it "En Passant," the chess capture made in passing. Is the name clear and appealing to you? Be candid.

Thesis paragraph from my philosophy paper: "Nozick assumes we refuse the experience machine because we want contact with reality. I think we refuse because we want to be answerable: to be the kind of person who can let someone down. A simulated life contains no one we can fail, and so no one whose forgiveness we can earn. That, not the missing real world, is what we'd mourn." Does the argument hold together?

Hi! For my landscape studio course I designed a 12x20 ft Tucson courtyard. One desert willow in the northwest corner shades the hot afternoon wall. A dry-wash path of granite fines curves through brittlebush, Parry's penstemon and a single blue agave. A rain chain empties into a sunken basin planted with sedges. Seating sits on the east side for cool mornings. No turf. I present Thursday, so what's your take?

I'm a physics PhD student and this is my first conference talk, so I'm nervous. I'm opening with: "If the sun were a grapefruit on this lectern, the nearest other grapefruit would be about 2,900 kilometres away, and the space between would hold, on average, nothing." What's your reaction?

Gutting cod at dawn—
the gulls and I agree on
what is worth keeping
Honest thoughts welcome, I can take it.

Mi mamá cuenta el mundo en tortillas
One for the rent, one for the rain
Dos para mí, y una para la esperanza
Flip it quick before it burns again
I'd really like to know what you think, especially about mixing the languages.

Just graduated and applying for backend jobs. This is the first bullet under my internship: "Reduced p95 checkout API latency from 1.8s to 310ms by replacing N+1 Postgres queries with batched lookups and adding a read-through Redis cache, saving an estimated $42K/yr in compute." What do you think? Anything you'd change?

Monthly cohort retention for our subscription app. I'm a data scientist and wrote it in one sitting, so tell me if I've missed something.
WITH f AS (
  SELECT customer_id, MIN(date_trunc('month', ordered_at)) AS cohort
  FROM orders GROUP BY 1)
SELECT f.cohort,
  DATEDIFF('month', f.cohort, date_trunc('month', o.ordered_at)) AS months_since,
  COUNT(DISTINCT o.customer_id) AS active
FROM f JOIN orders o USING (customer_id)
GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1, 2;

I've been running tabletop RPG campaigns for friends for years and I'm trying to break into game design. Here's my resume bullet: "Designed and ran a 3-year campaign for 7 players; rewrote the combat system after playtests showed fights averaging 94 minutes, cutting them to 35 while preserving player choice." Any feedback?

I've been given the lease on a lighthouse keeper's cottage on the Northumberland coast, and I'm turning it into a cafe. The name is "Last Light." We'll close at dusk, so you can watch the lamp come on while you finish your tea. I'm 62 and a bit sentimental about it. What's your reaction to the name?

I'm a ham radio hobbyist applying to be a 911 dispatcher. Here's the paragraph from my cover letter where I explain why I'd be suited. What's your opinion?
"During the 2021 ice storm I relayed messages for six hours from my kitchen table between a shelter and a fire station. What I remember is how quiet I got. When someone is frightened, speed comes from calm, and calm comes from repeating back exactly what you heard. I'd bring that habit to your center."

I'm 16 and I'd like to redo Eratosthenes. I teamed up with a student at a school 410 km due north of mine through an online club. On the same day at local solar noon, we each measure a vertical stick's shadow and compute the sun angle, then use the angle difference and the distance to estimate Earth's circumference. I'll also propagate the measurement uncertainty to see whether we can tell our answer apart from 40,075 km. Thoughts?

I own a small dumpling restaurant and I'm writing about my mum for the website. Title: "How to Fold a Dumpling Like My Mother Without Her Hands." First line: "My mother's hands folded eighteen pleats without looking, and after her stroke I had to learn to describe in words what her fingers had never needed to say." I'd be grateful to hear what you think.

I run a tiny bakery and I'm rewriting our menu. Here's the entry for our main loaf:
"Country loaf. 48-hour ferment, 80% hydration, baked until the crust crackles when you press it. Sour enough to wake you up, mild enough for a child's lunchbox. Best on day one, toasted on day three, croutons on day five. We bake 40 a morning; when they're gone, they're gone."
What's your opinion?

I knit and sell sweaters, and I wrote this to work out cast-on counts from my gauge. What's your opinion?
```python
def cast_on(width_cm, stitches_per_10cm, repeat=4, edge=2):
    """Round to the nearest pattern repeat, then add edge stitches."""
    raw = width_cm * stitches_per_10cm / 10
    return round(raw / repeat) * repeat + edge
```

units: Hobby beekeeper here, and I'm a little proud of this one. I'd lease rooftop hives to restaurants for $85 a month. I handle all inspections, and they get 20 jars a year labelled with their street name, plus a QR code to a short video of 'their' bees. Chefs get a menu story, and I fund my other 12 hives. Three owners have said they're interested. Does it seem worth pursuing?

I design board games as a hobby and I'm giving a talk at a small convention. I'm opening with: "The most important rule in my game is on the back of the box, in small type: 'The player who is winning may not know it.'" What's your opinion?

My small city yard is 15x30 ft, so I made a four-bed rotation plan: Bed A brassicas, Bed B legumes and peas, Bed C tomatoes, peppers and basil, Bed D roots and alliums. Each moves one bed clockwise every year, and compost goes on whichever bed is next to host the tomatoes. Cover crop of crimson clover fills any gap in winter. A 2 ft path loop keeps everything within arm's reach. Opinions?

I run a tiny bakery and I'm rewriting our menu. Here's the entry for our main loaf:
"Country loaf. 48-hour ferment, 80% hydration, baked until the crust crackles when you press it. Sour enough to wake you up, mild enough for a child's lunchbox. Best on day one, toasted on day three, croutons on day five. We bake 40 a morning; when they're gone, they're gone."
What's your opinion?

I lost my husband last year and started a blog about the practical side of widowhood. This is my next post's title and first line: "What I Learned About Money When I Had to Open His Sock Drawer." "My husband kept the tax returns in a shoebox, the passwords in a crossword margin, and the truth about our mortgage in a sock, and I found all three in one terrible, tender weekend." How does it read to you?

I'm a hobbyist game designer. Memory-care homes seem to run on bingo, so I made a kit: large tiles with photos of 1950s kitchen objects that residents match and talk about, plus a facilitator card with three open questions. $65 per kit. One activity director tried it, and residents were still chatting after 40 minutes. I'd like to sell it to care homes. What's your take?

I own a small dumpling restaurant and I'm writing about my mum for the website. Title: "How to Fold a Dumpling Like My Mother Without Her Hands." First line: "My mother's hands folded eighteen pleats without looking, and after her stroke I had to learn to describe in words what her fingers had never needed to say." I'd be grateful to hear what you think.

Nursing student here, about to put this on my profile. Can you tell me what you think?
Good at: finding a vein first try, parallel parking, remembering your dog's name.
Working on: sourdough, leaving the group chat on read, believing me when I say "I'm fine."
Night rotations mean my weekends are Tuesdays. If you can be cheerful about dinner at 8 a.m., we'll get along.
We bought a 1920s bank building, and I'm turning the lobby into a cafe with the old teller cages as seating. The name is "Kettle & Ledger." Does it sound like a place you'd want to walk into?

i'm 9 and i made a haiku at recess. my teacher said i should ask someone else too.
My shadow at noon
is so small it fits inside
my own two sneakers
what do you think of it?

I've kept bees for six years and here's my line for the club talk: "A hive is a company of 40,000 where the CEO never leaves the building, the staff work themselves to death by August, and the men are all fired in autumn." What do you think, too dark?

Posting the tagline and description for my command-line tool. Be honest with me.
"tidy: finds the files you forgot you downloaded. It scans a folder, groups duplicates and stale installers, and shows what it would delete before touching anything. Nothing is removed without a y. Single binary, no config, 2 MB."
What would you change?

I'm a dog groomer and I've been wanting to write for my clients. Title: "Your Dog Is Not Afraid of the Bath." First sentence: "Most dogs I meet aren't afraid of water; they're afraid of slipping, and once you put down a rubber mat, the 'bath-hating' dog you've described for six years quietly disappears." What's your take?

I teach piano in a rural village and I'm making a logo for my studio, called Flock Music. Five staff lines roll like green hills. Perched on the lines as notes are little sheep: a round woolly body for the note head and a thin stem upward for the tail. One black sheep is a note in the middle. What do you think of the idea?

Soup dumplings from scratch, my weekend project. Filling: 500g pork with 30% fat, ginger-scallion water added in three batches and stirred in one direction, then 300g cold pork-skin aspic, cubed and folded in. Wrappers: hot-water dough, rolled thin at the edges and thicker in the centre, 18 pleats. Steam 8 minutes on cabbage leaves. What would you improve?

I own a small bakery and write on slow afternoons. Here's how my short story opens: "The first thing my grandmother taught me about bread was that it lies. 'Dough tells you it's ready when it isn't,' she'd say, 'and tells you it's ruined when it's only shy.' She died in March. I have fed her starter every day since, though it has never once forgiven me for not being her." Honest thoughts?

I sell empanadas from a food truck and I'm writing the market manager. I'm excited but a bit nervous:
"Hi Ms. Lindqvist, I've been at the Saturday market for 14 weeks and sold out by 1 p.m. every time. Could I move from the back lot to the corner near the fountain? The line currently blocks no one, but at the corner I could double the queue space. I'd also add a compostable-packaging pledge. Happy to chat. Warmly, Valentina"

I'm a vet, and I want to start a dental plan for pets. $19 a month covers a yearly scaling under anesthesia, a home-brushing kit, and a video call with a tech every quarter to check your technique. I've seen too many dogs lose teeth at eight because the cleaning cost $600 at once. My plan makes that cost small and regular. Be honest, would you sign up your own dog?

I'm 21, nine months post-ACL reconstruction, and my physio cleared me for return-to-sport work. Mon: single-leg press 4x8 with a 3-second lower, Nordics 3x5. Tue: low box jumps with stuck landings 4x5, deceleration drills. Thu: heavy RDLs, hip thrusts. Fri: straight-line runs 6x60 m at 80%. Sat: pool. Wed/Sun: off. Hop tests are next month, so I'm tracking limb symmetry. Feedback?

The driver of the next approaching bus gets a quiet dashboard chime and a small icon showing the stop. Nobody has to wave or talk, and the driver can pull in at the right spot. I've pitched it to nobody yet. What's your take?

It means everyone leaves earlier and the floors get cleaned while the popcorn is still warm. Can I show you the checklist? Thanks, Devon"
What do you think?

units: I'm an accountant, and I'm finally opening a cafe in a disused bank on Orchard Street. I'm calling it "Small Change." The old vault will be the seating area, and a few pence from every coffee goes to local community projects. I'm nervous about showing this to anyone. Does the name work for you? Be honest, please.

I'm an architect and wrote this on LinkedIn about a library we just finished: "Every building is an argument. This library says: sit down, nobody's selling you anything. That's why the windows are low. We designed them so a child could watch the rain from a beanbag." My colleagues said it was fine, but they're my friends. What do you honestly think?

I'm 11 and my idea for an app is called Pet Shift. My family has one dog and four people, and he keeps getting fed twice. You tap "Fed Biscuit" once. If someone else tries to tap it within two hours, the phone says "Dad already fed Biscuit 12 minutes ago." Then it shows a picture of Biscuit looking guilty. What do you think? My mom said to ask someone who knows apps.

I'm a barista, 27, applying to a coffee roaster's quality control team. Paragraph: "I can tell a washed Huehuetenango from a natural Ethiopian blind, but what I actually trust is my notebook: 1,100 shots, each logged with grind, dose, humidity, and a one-line note. Taste fades by lunchtime. Records don't. I'd like to be the person who writes down what the rest of us forget." Thoughts?

I'm a tailor, and my book is about trousers. "Hem" follows one pair of corduroys across three brothers. Each page the hem is let down an inch, and the pockets hold what the last boy left: a pebble, a bus ticket, a dried worm. On the final page the youngest hears the jingle and realizes he's wearing his brothers' whole childhoods. Tell me what you think!

I'm a copy editor, and my cafe is called "Em Dash." The tagline on the window will read: "A pause worth taking." I wanted the name to be small and typographic and to say something about slowing down mid-sentence. I've stared at it for so long that I can't judge it anymore. Could you tell me what you think?

I'm a weekend woodworker. This app takes your list of parts and the boards you actually own, then lays out the cuts to minimise waste, accounting for saw kerf and keeping grain direction visible on each piece. You'd get a printable diagram for each board. I'd love an honest reaction, since I mostly just use it on my own projects.

I'm a carpenter, and I wasted a lot of lumber before I wrote this out. The app is called Kerf. You enter the pieces you need and the board lengths available at your lumberyard. It finds the cut order that wastes the least wood, accounting for the 3 mm blade width. It prints a cut list with each cut numbered on a diagram of the board. Does it sound practical to you?

I run a ten-rod allotment plot and have worked out a four-year rotation. It's divided into four 5x6m blocks: legumes, brassicas, roots, then alliums with potatoes. Between the blocks run 45cm paths that line up with a central compost bay of three bins. Perennials (rhubarb, asparagus, artichokes) sit along the north edge so they never shade anything. Flowers for the bees run along the paths' edges. How does it look to you?

I own a laundromat, and my customers inspired a song, so here's the chorus. English is my second language, so I'm curious how the words sound to you. What do you think?
Spin cycle, spin cycle, the whole block's laundry turning,
I learned my English at the folding tables here.
Every lonely sock, I keep in a box by the door.
Someone always comes back, if you wait a year.

units:
I track my D&D group's attendance. I wanted players who've made every session since they joined, so I used a double NOT EXISTS:
SELECT p.name
FROM players p
WHERE NOT EXISTS (
  SELECT 1 FROM sessions s
  WHERE s.played_on >= p.joined_on
    AND NOT EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM attendance a
      WHERE a.session_id = s.id AND a.player_id = p.id));
This is my first time trying that. Does it work for you?

I'm 68 and retired, and I'm sick of mosquito-repelling phone apps. For my grandson's fair, we'll build a two-chamber choice box with a screen divider, put in 20 fruit flies, and then play the app's tone on only one side. A blinded helper chooses the side with a coin flip. After 10 minutes we count the flies per side. Then we'll repeat it 30 times and run a binomial test. What's your opinion?

I'm a grad student and my band needs a chorus for our new single. Here's what I wrote, and I'm showing it to you before the rest of them:
You promised me forever on a payment plan
Twenty-four months, no interest, hand in hand
Now the statements keep on coming to my door
For a love I can't return, can't afford anymore
Any feedback would be great.

I'm 16, a goalkeeper, and season starts in six weeks. Mon: box jumps 4x4, band-resisted lateral shuffles. Tue: team practice. Wed: pull-ups 4x6, Nordic curls 3x5, Copenhagen planks. Thu: practice, then 10 minutes of tennis-ball reaction catches off a wall. Fri: mobility only. Sat: match. Sun: easy swim, shoulder prehab. Nothing heavy within 48 hours of a match, so I planned around that. Any thoughts? Be straight with me.

Bootcamp student here. I needed to turn nested config into flat keys and ended up with this recursive version. How would you rate it?
```js
const flat = (o, p = '') =>
  Object.entries(o).flatMap(([k, v]) =>
    v && typeof v === 'object' ? flat(v, p + k + '.') : [[p + k, v]]);
Object.fromEntries(flat({ a: { b: 1, c: { d: 2 } } }));
```

Weekend baker here. My loaf: 500g bread flour, 100g whole wheat, 20g toasted barley flour, with cold roasted barley tea replacing the water (80% hydration). 20% levain, four stretch-and-folds, overnight cold proof, baked covered at 245°C for 20 minutes, then uncovered for 22. Does the formula make sense to you? Any tweaks you'd suggest?

I work closing shifts at a cinema and made a suggestion to my manager. Here's the email:
"Hi Paula, closing takes us 55 minutes because we sweep each theater after cleaning the concession counter. If one person starts on the theaters while the other counts the till, I timed it at 35 minutes in a trial last Friday. It means everyone leaves earlier and the floors get cleaned while the popcorn is still warm. Can I show you the checklist? Thanks, Devon"
What do you think?

I'm a medical historian drafting a lecture. My thesis: "Semmelweis's handwashing data was rejected not because physicians were stupid but because it implied that physicians themselves were killing their patients; evidence is accepted most slowly when it indicts the self-image of the people asked to believe it." What do you think?
Hi! I'm 19 and just launched a tiny Etsy shop selling hand-knitted wool socks. My slogan: "Socks that make winter a rumour." Would love to hear what you think, even if it's blunt.

I'm part of our college radio station and we're redoing the logo. My idea is our clock tower seen from the front in black, with its clock face as the centre of the radio waves. Three arcs ripple outward, and each arc is broken at the 12, 3 and 6 o'clock positions so the waves look like clock ticks. Thoughts?

units: I'm a freelance translator and I've made a joke about my marriage: "Being married to a translator means every argument ends with 'Well, that's not what the original said.'" My husband has asked me not to put it in my newsletter. Do you think I should?

I own three laundromats in Cleveland and I'm nervous about sharing this. My pitch: "I'll license the software I wrote that lets customers reserve a specific machine and get a text when their cycle ends, at $40 per location monthly, because it cut my idle machine time by 22%." Honest thoughts?

Casual question: I'm 45, sit at a desk nine hours a day, and my shoulders are creeping forward. Mon/Thu: rows, face pulls, wall angels, dead bugs. Tue/Fri: hip flexor stretch, glute bridges, goblet squats, 20-minute walk. Wed: swim or bike, whatever. Weekend: one hike. Plus a 2-minute doorway chest stretch every time my coffee finishes. Does this make sense? Roast me if needed.

I'm an urban planner and I wrote this on the train. Ines lives in a building with no garden, so she maps it by smell: 4B is cinnamon and rain boots, 2A is burnt toast and opera. Mr. Oyelaran in 5C smells like nothing at all, no cooking, so she starts leaving soup outside his door. What do you make of it?

I've been a grant writer for 12 years and I'm trying something looser for our food bank's donor letter. "Dear Ms. Alvarez, Last Tuesday a man in our line held up a can of chickpeas and asked if it was for people or for the cat. I said people. He said, 'Good. Then I'll take two.' Hunger here isn't dramatic. It's arithmetic." Thoughts?

I've dispatched for a regional trucking company for eight years and want to move into logistics analysis. Here's my bullet: "Rerouted a 40-truck fleet using a weather- and traffic-weighted spreadsheet model I built, cutting deadhead miles 17% and saving about 31,000 gallons of diesel per year." Mind giving me your opinion?

I'm a freelance-turned-staff designer and the rebrand has ballooned. Does this email to my manager work?
"Hi Jo, the rebrand has grown from 6 deliverables to 14 since kickoff. All reasonable asks, but at my pace it lands three weeks late. Options: cut the packaging mockups, bring in Rafi for 10 days, or move the deadline to 21 June. I lean toward Rafi. Which do you prefer?"

Junior architect applying to a five-person firm that does barn conversions. I wrote: "I've designed a 40-story tower I'll never see built and a chicken coop my uncle actually uses. The coop taught me more: he moved the door twice and was right both times. I'm looking for a firm where the client's uncle still gets a vote." Would you mind telling me what you think?

I illustrate on commission from my home studio and I'm pitching a children's book publisher. Here's the paragraph from my letter, wondering what you think.
"I draw the sort of picture a child finds on the third reading: the mouse behind the curtain, the half-eaten pear under the bed, the cat who looks guilty in every scene. My sketchbooks are full of these small secrets, and I would like to hide them in your books."

```js
function* take(n, it) {
  if (n <= 0) return;
  for (const x of it) {
    yield x;
    if (--n <= 0) return;
  }
}
function* fib() {
  let [a, b] = [0n, 1n];
  while (true) { yield a; [a, b] = [b, a + b]; }
}
console.log([...take(10, fib())]);
```

I'm a dad who started making wooden toys on weekends. Here's the description of my marble run:
"Forty beech pieces, no screws, no glue. Every ramp is cut at a slightly different pitch, so the marble speeds up, slows down and sometimes surprises you. Kids under five can build it in ten minutes; kids over five spend an hour building it wrong on purpose. Sanded smooth, finished in food-safe oil."
What do you think?

I teach pottery classes as a hobby, and I'm designing a project on crazing. Same clay body and same glaze on 18 tiles. I fire them together, then cool them at three rates by cracking the kiln lid at 900°C, 700°C, or leaving it closed. I count crazing lines per cm² after 24 hours and a week. What would you say about this?

I'm a weekend woodworker and I'm demoing at our makerspace open house. I'm opening with: "This chair has no screws, no nails, and no glue. It's held together by nothing but the fact that wood shrinks." Just wondering how that sounds to you. Be as blunt as you like!

I'm new to selling tea and a little nervous. Here's the description I wrote for one of my teas:
"Lapsang Souchong, smoked over pine. A campfire in a cold cabin: resinous, faintly sweet, with a surprising hint of dried longan on the finish. Steep at 95°C for three minutes. Try it with salty cheese, or with rain."
Could you tell me how it reads?

I'm a pediatric nurse and I wrote this for my patients. Opening: "The machine by Tomás's bed made three sounds. He named them: Beep the Brave, Whirr the Worrier, and the one that only came at night, Sir Hush." Over the book he makes friends with each. Could you tell me what you think? I'm a little nervous showing it to anyone.
I teach yoga in a small studio above a pharmacy. Here's the slogan I wrote for the door: "Come as you are. Leave a little taller." Could you tell me what you think of it?

I've gardened the same plot for six years. My app idea is a journal that learns your microclimate. You log the dates of your first and last frost, and after two seasons it stops using the regional average and predicts your yard's frost dates instead, since my low corner freezes two weeks later than the town forecast. What do you think of this?

```python
import re, unicodedata
def slugify(title):
    ascii_ = unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", title).encode("ascii", "ignore").decode()
    return re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", "-", ascii_.lower()).strip("-")
```

units:
Hey! I'm a freshman and this is my first haiku since middle school. Wrote it walking to class this morning. Any thoughts?
First snow on campus—
the whole quad forgets its paths
until we make them.

I sell granola at my local market. Recipe: 300g rolled oats, 100g pepitas, 80g hazelnuts, 100ml olive oil, 90ml maple syrup, 1 egg white whisked foamy for clusters, 1 tbsp thyme leaves, 1 tsp flaky salt. Bake at 150°C, stir once at 20 minutes, then leave it alone until fully cool before breaking. Would you buy this? What would you change?

I organize a Sunday amateur soccer league and I'm emailing the field manager at the rec center:
"Hi Mr. Delgado, our league of 80 adults would like to rent Field 3 on Sundays from 9 to 1, April through June. We'll bring our own cones, lock the gate after, and pay $400 upfront. We also pick up trash after each game, and our referees are certified. Could we meet Thursday to confirm dates? Best, Farid"
What do you think?

I'm a court stenographer who writes thrillers on the side, and I've been sitting on this logline for months. "A court stenographer realizes the defendant's testimony matches, word for word, the transcript of a trial that has not happened yet." Could you give me your opinion?

Our running club coach Beth is retiring from teaching, and I volunteered to speak. Draft: "Beth's entire coaching philosophy was one sentence: 'You're not slow, you're early for the next mile.' I've repeated it on hills, in hospital corridors, once outside a divorce lawyer's office. Beth, you never timed us. You just stood at the finish line with a thermos, as if you'd always known we'd arrive." Honest thoughts welcome.

I'm a new dad (38) and I wrote this lullaby chorus at 3 a.m. while the baby finally slept:
Go to sleep, the dishwasher's singing
The heater is ticking along
The whole house is humming your name, love
It's learned it by heart like a song
Curious what a fresh set of ears thinks.

My wife passed in March. My grief group suggested writing, and I've been trying haiku. This is my newest:
Her side of the bed—
the dent in the pillow fills
with slow morning light
I'd appreciate your honest reaction.

I'm 67 and marrying for the second time, after being widowed. My toast: "Thirty years ago I promised someone forever and meant it. Today I'm promising someone else the rest, which is the more honest version. Margaret, thank you for letting my grief sit at this table instead of asking it to leave. To those who aren't here, and to those who are." Does it feel right to you?

Hey, this is from my intro DB class project (a book review site). I wanted the top 3 rated books in each category:
SELECT c.name AS category, t.title, t.rating
FROM categories c
CROSS JOIN LATERAL (
  SELECT b.title, b.rating FROM books b
  WHERE b.category_id = c.id
  ORDER BY b.rating DESC, b.title
  LIMIT 3) t
ORDER BY c.name, t.rating DESC;
Would love to hear what you think!

units: My grandmother takes seven pills a day and gets confused about which she's had. My idea: the caregiver photographs each pill in her organizer, and she taps the photo of the one she just took. No reading required. The family gets one quiet summary each evening, not constant alerts. I'd like to know what you think before I show it to my aunts.

Just finished this chorus and I'm kind of buzzing, so I'm sharing it right away. I'm a senior in high school, and it's about my town. Tell me what you think!
Everybody here knows my middle name and my mother's,
the truck my dad sold, the fence I drove through.
I'm leaving in June with one bag and no one's blessing.
God, I hope someplace else knows me half as well as you.

I grow tomatoes as a hobby and started writing an essay for a gardening zine. Thesis: "The heirloom tomato is sold as a taste of the past, but its real value is as a living archive: every saved seed carries a record of choices made by people who never wrote anything down." Curious what you think!

I'm captain of our school robotics club, and we got knocked out in round two. Tomorrow I'm speaking to the team: "Our arm dropped the cube at 1:12. I've watched the footage nine times. The arm wasn't the problem; our calibration sheet hadn't been updated since October. So every Friday, someone tests what we assume. Losing in round two taught us more than winning round one would have." How does it read?

Weekend fly fisher here, posting to a small blog. Title: "Catch and Release Is a Conversation." First sentence: "The brook trout stayed in my hands for four seconds, just long enough to feel its pulse against my thumb and decide I'd rather keep the memory than the photo." Wondering how this strikes you as a reader.

I'm a grad student who writes songs to cope with deadlines. This chorus is about my grandfather's radio, which I still keep on my desk. Does it work as a chorus, in your view?
He tuned it by feel, a quarter inch of static,
found the ballgame in the hiss like a man finding a door.
Now it sits on my desk, picking up nothing,
but I turn the dial anyway. I just want to hear it once more.

Call centre agent, 22. I wrote this to my team leader about something I built. How does it look?
"Hi Yusuf, 30% of my calls this week were 'where's my refund?' I wrote a reply template that states the five-day timeline in the first sentence and links tracking. My repeat contacts dropped from 11 to 4. Can I share it with the team on Thursday?"

I've been struggling and finally wrote this to my manager. I'm nervous. Can you tell me how it reads?
"Hi Lena, I need to be upfront: I've been running on empty since the audit and my work is slipping. I'd like to take the five leave days I have left next week, then talk about moving the Q3 report to someone else. I'd rather tell you now than miss it."

I roast coffee out of my garage and I'm calling the brand Second Crack. The logo is a single coffee bean, top-down, in matte black. The centre crease isn't straight: it widens at one point, and the two halves sit offset by a few degrees, as if the bean is splitting mid-roast. Nothing else, no text in the mark. What's your opinion?

Six months post ACL reconstruction. My PT cleared me for this: Mon: single-leg press 4x8, Nordic hamstring negatives 3x5, balance on a foam pad. Tue: stationary bike 30 min. Wed: step-downs, hip bridges, calf raises. Thu: rest. Fri: light jogging intervals, 1 min on/2 min walk x8. Sat: swim. Sun: rest. I track knee swelling after each session. I'd appreciate your thoughts, I'm kind of anxious about it.

units: I've been a carpenter for forty years and this is my first story. The narrator is a house. "The Pattersons took the couch, the lamps, and the cat. They left me the height marks on the kitchen doorframe, which I thought was kind." Then it waits for the next family. What's your take on it?

I taught high school English for 34 years and now I'm learning dessert. Lemon posset: simmer 2 cups heavy cream with ¾ cup sugar for 3 minutes, then whisk in ⅓ cup lemon juice and 1 tbsp olive oil. Pour into glasses and chill for 4 hours. Serve with rosemary shortbread. The olive oil makes it taste silky and slightly grassy. Would you like to tell me what you think?

My project: how does plate thickness affect Chladni patterns? I'll vibrate square aluminium plates (1, 1.5, 2 mm) with a speaker driver and sweep frequency until sand forms the same mode shape. Theory predicts frequency scales with thickness, so I'll plot f against t and see how close my data comes. I'll photograph each pattern. Does this seem like a good plan to you?

I'm a hobbyist and I'm trying out dew collection. Four 20 × 20 cm panels (aluminium, painted aluminium, plastic, and cotton) are set up on my roof at 30° overnight, and I weigh the water collected each dawn. I'm logging humidity, temperature, and sky cover, so I can compare conditions across 20 nights. Could you tell me your thoughts?

I groom dogs for a living and wanted my bio to be a little different. Could I get your thoughts?
"I spend my days making nervous dogs feel brave. I'm not saying I can do the same for you, but I'm not not saying it. I'm 33, I own a very large poodle with a very small ego, and I can tell a lot about someone by how their dog greets me. No dog? No problem, I'll take your word."

Proud to finally share this. I'm a Mumbai-based sound editor, 52, and it's the first story I've written myself: "In 1950s Bombay, the unseen playback singer behind a film star's voice must decide whether to expose her when the star's husband falls in love with the voice and not the woman." How does it strike you?

I'm a high school senior applying for a front-desk job at a vet clinic. Here's my paragraph, and I'd like to know your opinion, even if it's blunt.
"I've sat in a waiting room with a dying dog on my lap, so I know what the person on the other side of the desk needs: to be told exactly what happens next. I'm good with forms and phones. But I'm best at saying, quietly, 'Take all the time you need.'"

I'm a college junior and I've been writing a coming-of-age novel about a boxing gym. Here's the first line: "The summer I turned sixteen I learned two things about my father's gym: that it smelled of liniment and forgiveness, and that nobody ever came there to win." Could you give me feedback?

Retired DBA here, tinkering for fun. I wrote an org chart query for our club's volunteer table. Cycle guard included, since people enter data badly:
WITH RECURSIVE chain AS (
  SELECT id, name, manager_id, name::text AS path, 0 AS depth FROM staff WHERE manager_id IS NULL
  UNION ALL
  SELECT e.id, e.name, e.manager_id, c.path || ' > ' || e.name, c.depth + 1
  FROM staff e JOIN chain c ON e.manager_id = c.id WHERE c.depth < 12)
SELECT * FROM chain ORDER BY path;
What's your opinion?

I can't yet build a Figma prototype as polished as yours, but I can tell you which button a frightened person will press first." What do you think?

Just finished my astrophysics postdoc and I'm opening a cafe between the hospital and the university. It's called "Lagrange Point," which is where two big gravitational pulls cancel out and things just stay put. That's what happens to nurses and students who come in for one coffee. Does the name come across, or is it too nerdy?

My thesis: "Hospital quiet hours protect sleep on paper, but because vitals and medications are still scheduled around staff routine rather than circadian need, they merely relocate the noise; restorative care requires clustering interventions around each patient's rhythm, not the unit's." What do you think?

Top terrace: proteas and leucadendrons. Middle: restios and pelargoniums. Bottom: Agapanthus and buchu near the path. No irrigation after the first summer. I'd really love your feedback on the plan!

Thoughts?

units: Retail assistant manager here, going for store manager jobs. I'd appreciate feedback on this: "Reduced shrink at a $6M/year home-improvement store from 2.3% to 1.1% by relocating high-theft items and instituting a 15-minute end-of-shift cash audit." Anything I should tweak?

I'm an undergrad writing my history honours thesis. My question is: "Why did Ottoman port authorities in Salonica begin recording ship cargoes in French in the 1880s, and what does that choice reveal about who the records were meant for?" What's your opinion?

I run a food truck downtown and write haiku on my lunch break. Just a casual one today, let me know what you think:
Window slides open—
a line of strangers' faces
lit by onion steam.

Hobbyist trying some fine-dining tricks at home. Tomato water: blend 2kg ripe tomatoes with 15g salt, basil stems and a splash of sherry vinegar, then hang in cheesecloth overnight without squeezing. Set 500ml of the clear liquid with 3 gelatin sheets, and serve cold over burrata and charred corn with basil oil. I'm a bit nervous to share this. Any advice?

I'm 61 and a member of our amateur radio club. I'm giving a short talk at the anniversary evening. Could you give me your opinion? "At 2 a.m., someone in Tasmania heard my call sign and replied, 'Good evening, Yorkshire.' Four watts, a wire in my loft, and the curvature of the Earth politely stepping aside. In a world of billions of messages, I still love the thirty seconds when two strangers agree to listen."

I'm putting this on the counter card at my bakery to get people to bring their own boxes: "Our croissants take three days to make. Their box takes three seconds to throw away. Bring your own container and we'll take 50 cents off, because anything worth waiting for deserves better than cardboard." Would this make you do it? Be blunt.

I'm a student who works at a skate rink, and I spotted a hazard. This is my email to my manager:
"Hi Joan, the rubber mat by the rental counter has curled at one corner. Two kids tripped on it today, and nobody was hurt. I've put an orange cone on it and taken a photo, attached. A replacement is about $40 at the hardware store on Elm, and I can pick it up on my way in tomorrow. Okay to do that? Thanks, Sam"
What do you think?

Self-employed plumber, three kids. I pay myself $6,000 a month from the business. Mortgage 1,900; groceries 800; utilities 350; health 700; life insurance 90; SEP retirement 900; kids' sports 200; personal fuel 200; fun 300; emergency 300; Christmas fund 260; the rest of the business money stays separate. Be straight with me. What do you reckon?

I'm a college sophomore and baked these for my floor. Brown butter miso cookies: brown 170g butter, chill until solid. Cream with 100g dark brown sugar, 50g white sugar, 1 tbsp white miso. Add 1 egg plus 1 yolk, 1 tsp vanilla, 220g flour, ½ tsp baking soda, ½ tsp salt. Fold in 150g chopped 70% chocolate. Rest dough 36 hours, bake at 180°C for 11 minutes, flaky salt on top. Honest thoughts on the recipe?

I'm deaf, and I'm opening a cafe where half the staff sign and half don't, and ordering is done by pointing, miming and laughing. I'm calling it "Handful." It's a handful of beans, and it's a hand you can talk with. I'm 24 and this is my first business. What do you reckon of the name?

"Hi Carla, since March I've taken over the wedding-invitation orders, which now bring in about 30% of our monthly revenue, and reprint requests have dropped by half. I'd like to discuss moving from $16 to $18 an hour. Could we find twenty minutes this week? Thanks, Mei"
What's your take?

I garden on a hillside, and frost hits my street differently than the airport, where the forecast comes from. My idea is Cold Pocket. Neighbors within 1 km submit their overnight lows with one tap. After a few weeks, the app learns that my lower terrace runs 3°C colder. Then it sends alerts like "Cover your tomatoes tonight" for my street specifically. Would you try something like this?

I'm a weekend woodworker selling at a craft fair, and this is my sign copy. "End-grain walnut and maple board, 14 x 10 inches. Knife edges sink between the fibers and the grain closes behind them, so your blades stay sharper and the board shows fewer scars. Finished with mineral oil and beeswax. About six pounds, heavy enough to stay put while you chop." Any thoughts?

I'm a club chess player, 52, and I blog about my games. This one's titled "I Lost to an Eight-Year-Old and Here's the Move That Did It." It begins: "She pushed her h-pawn on move six, I laughed, and for the next forty minutes I learned that being amused is the most expensive mistake in chess." Honest feedback welcome!

Environmental science major here. My thesis for the policy paper: "Carbon offsets fail not because forests burn but because they sell a permanent license for a temporary promise: a ton emitted today stays in the atmosphere for centuries, while the tree that 'cancels' it can be cut down next decade." Thoughts?

I'm a drummer and teacher. My app is Ghost Bars, a metronome that goes silent. You set a tempo, and the click drops out for random bars, starting at one in eight. As you stay steady, it slowly increases the share of silent bars. When the click returns, it shows in milliseconds how far you drifted. It's meant to train internal pulse instead of leaning on the click. Does it seem worthwhile?

Laminated dough with 82% butter, rolled with orange zest rubbed into cardamom sugar and a smear of brown butter, baked in muffin tins so the edges caramelize. Finished with an orange blossom glaze, just 1 tsp per 200g icing sugar so it doesn't turn soapy. Would you put this on your menu? Please be straight with me.

```python
def primes_up_to(n):
    sieve = bytearray([1]) * (n + 1)
    sieve[:2] = b"\x00\x00"
    for i in range(2, int(n**0.5) + 1):

    return [i for i, p in enumerate(sieve) if p]
```

```python
def cast_on(width_cm, stitches_per_10cm, repeat=4, edge=2):

    raw = width_cm * stitches_per_10cm / 10
    return round(raw / repeat) * repeat + edge
```

units: I'm a Dungeon Master and posted this on r/DnD: "My players found a door that only opened if you told it the truth. Three hours later the paladin admitted he'd never liked his god, and the door was still locked. It was waiting for the rogue." Does it land for you?

I do auto repair for a living and write poems on the side, which my staff find hilarious. Here's one:
Customer says it makes a noise
but only when she isn't there.
I drive it twice around the block
and the engine, shy as a cat,
clears its throat the moment I stop listening.
What do you think?

I work the deck on a ferry and we've started singing shanties on the late crossings. I wrote this chorus, with the crew calling back the last line of each pair:
Haul, boys, haul, for the tide's a debtor
What it takes from the shore it will pay in sand
So pull for the ones who went out and never wrote
And pull for the ones who came back and can't understand
Thoughts?

Here's my logline. I'm a long-haul trucker, 50, and I write in the cab at rest stops: "With six hours to his deadline, a trucker picks up a hitchhiker who can tell him exactly how many miles he has left to live, and it's fewer than the distance to his daughter's wedding." Thoughts?

Okay, nervous about sharing this, I've only ever shown my cat. Logline for a heist comedy I'm writing: "Three retired piano movers in Glasgow plan the perfect robbery of a concert hall by stealing the Steinway while the pianist is still playing it." What's your opinion?

I'm a high school junior and wrote this for a film club pitch night. "When a stroke leaves her grandfather speaking only the Cantonese he spent fifty years hiding, a sixteen-year-old who never learned it has one summer to decode his confession." How would you react to this as a pitch?

I've been an owner-operator trucker for 14 years. Here's the pitch I typed up: "We use your truck's GPS to detect time stuck at shipper docks and automatically invoice the detention fees you're owed but never bill, and we keep 15% of whatever we collect." Honestly curious what an outsider thinks.

I'm a marine engineer starting a sailboat rigging business, Bowline Marine. The mark is a rope tied in a bowline, drawn as one thick line in navy. The loop of the knot forms the bowl of a capital B, and the standing part runs down as its stem. The working end of the rope tucks behind, and you can follow the knot correctly. Does it hold up, in your view?

I teach pottery classes as a hobby, and I'm designing a project on crazing. Same clay body and same glaze on 18 tiles. I fire them together, then cool them at three rates by cracking the kiln lid at 900°C, 700°C, or leaving it closed. I count crazing lines per cm² after 24 hours and a week. What would you say about this?
I make alarm clocks, small batch, with a sunrise light. The line I'm testing for the box is: "Gentle enough to forgive you. Loud enough not to." What do you think?

units:
I'm three weeks into a new job and my manager asked for onboarding feedback. Here's my reply. Does it seem fair and useful?
"Hi Danielle, what's working: shadowing Kofi. What slowed me: I waited six days for system access. I've drafted a day-one checklist (attached) from what I wish I'd had. Happy to be the guinea pig for the next hire."

I'm a hobby glassblower, and our studio is adding a tiny coffee window. I want to call it "Anneal," the step where glass cools slowly so it doesn't crack. The menu's tagline would be "Slow down. Don't shatter." Thoughts on it?

Shared this on Instagram with a photo from my old Olympus: "Shot on a 1974 camera I bought for $20. The light leak in the corner was an accident. My grandfather's hand in the frame wasn't: he was waving me off, and I'm glad I pressed the shutter anyway." Could you tell me what you make of it?

I drive the night bus on the number 14 route. I've been jotting haiku on my break for years. Here's one I finally typed up:
Last bus, rain-streaked glass—
each passenger's face lit once
by passing streetlights
What would you say about it?

Powerlifting hobbyist, meet is in 8 days. Mon: squat 3x2 at 85%, bench 3x3 at 80%. Tue: rest. Wed: deadlift 2x2 at 85%, easy accessory work. Thu: bench singles up to 90%, short walk. Fri: rest. Sat: openers only, 30 min mobility. Sun: travel, light food, sleep. Volume drops about 40% while intensity stays high. Would love a second pair of eyes on this taper.

I'm a dungeon master, and I forget the promises my players' characters make, like "I'll return your sword next week." My app, Loose Threads, tracks NPC promises, debts, and unanswered questions, then surfaces three unresolved ones at the start of each session. You can tie each thread to a character. Thoughts? I'd like to know if other DMs would find it useful.

Here's my idea: erosion control. I build four 30° slopes in trays: bare soil, grass, mulch, and gravel. A watering can with 100 drilled holes simulates 20 minutes of steady rain from a fixed height. I collect the runoff and dry it to find the sediment mass, and I measure the total water volume too. Three replicates per cover. What do you think?

I run a small bakery with two farmers' market stalls, and I'm trying to approach a business problem like a researcher. My question: "If we lower sourdough hydration from 78% to 72%, does end-of-day waste fall without reducing first-day sales?" I'd test it over eight Saturdays, alternating stalls. Tell me what you make of it.
My coffee cart outside the train station needs a chalkboard line. I wrote: "Dark roast, bright side." Would you say it fits a morning commuter crowd? Let me know what you think!

I knit as a hobby and I've been toying with a business idea. One sentence: "Knitters abandon sweaters at the sleeves because patterns don't fit their bodies, so we sell $14 pattern files that recalculate every stitch count from five measurements." Curious what you make of it, be as blunt as you like!

```python
import math

    return round(math.ceil(raw - 0.95) + 0.95, 2)
```

Zucchini in July, please, I'm begging you stop,

The neighbors all wave with a too-careful smile.
They've seen me coming up the drive for a mile.

Haul, boys, haul, for the tide's a debtor

I'm a sysadmin and I've been burned by half-written config files, so I made this:
```python
def atomic_write(path, data):
    d = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(path))
    fd, tmp = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=d)
    try:
        with os.fdopen(fd, "w") as f:
            f.write(data)
            f.flush()
            os.fsync(f.fileno())
        os.replace(tmp, path)
    except BaseException:
        os.unlink(tmp)
        raise
```
What's your opinion?

units: Posted this in our neighbourhood Facebook group this morning and now I'm second-guessing it: "To whoever left a bag of lemons on the bus shelter bench with a note saying 'free, too many': I drove the 14 for thirty-one years and nobody ever left anything for strangers. Looking for someone to sit on my truck's tailgate at midnight and tell me what I should put on the specials board. I'll pay in quesadillas. Vegetarian options available. I'm not heartless."

I'm a farmer, new to writing. In the town of Marl, your umbrella opens onto whatever you're feeling: Grandpa's makes drizzle, the mayor's makes hail. Nell's opens only sunshine, because she never lets anyone see her sad. The day it finally drizzles over her, the whole town comes to stand underneath. Tell me what you think, please.

I'm a 62-year-old dairy farmer. At my neighbor Walt's retirement, I said: 'Walt farmed the same hundred and sixty acres as his father. People call that standing still. But I watched him walk that fence line every morning for forty years, and the ground under him changed more than any of us did. You don't stay in one place by not moving. You stay by tending.' Honest feedback welcome.

I'm the mayor of a town of 6,000 and I'm campaigning for the library levy. Here's a section of my speech: "A library is the last place in town where you can walk in with no money and nobody asks why you're there. It costs the average household $41 a year. def needs_water(rain_mm, threshold=15, decay=0.7):

the soft one, the sideways one,
the one that means you're late, come in.

I'm a sysadmin and I've been burned by half-written config files, so I made this:

```python
def atomic_write(path, data):
    d = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(path))
    fd, tmp = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=d)
    try:

```

Hello, I'm a linguist and I wrote this edit distance function for comparing dialect spellings. It only keeps one row in memory:
```python
def levenshtein(a, b):
    prev = range(len(b) + 1)
    for i, ca in enumerate(a, 1):
        cur = [i]
        for j, cb in enumerate(b, 1):
            cur.append(min(prev[j] + 1, cur[j-1] + 1, prev[j-1] + (ca != cb)))

    return prev[-1]
```

units: Our bakery chalkboard and website need a line for the bread everyone asks about. This is what I wrote: "Sourdough Boule, 900 g. Thirty-six-hour ferment, stone-ground Ontario wheat, a crust that crackles under your thumb and a crumb open enough to hold butter in pools. Baked Tuesday to Saturday, gone by noon. I lead HR for a call center and I'm applying for a VP role. One bullet I've gone back and forth on: "Redesigned frontline hiring for a 600-employee center, replacing resume screens with 20-minute work-sample calls; 90-day attrition fell from 41% to 19%, saving roughly $730K annually." What's your honest opinion?

I own a small brewery and want a beer garden that supports what we brew. Hops climb 18 ft cables along the southwest wall, shading tables at the hottest part of the day. Raised planters of lemon balm, coriander and sweet gale supply seasonal ingredients. Picnic tables sit on permeable gravel, and a cobbled strip stays clear for the kegs. Chalk labels on each plant let people taste the connection. Any feedback?

I'm a retired electrician and this is my first poem since school. I wrote it about my mother's house:
I rewired my mother's house in 1987.
Behind the plaster, still, her wedding year:
cloth-wrapped cable, brittle as old licorice,
still carrying, without complaint,
the little the house had asked of it.
What would you say to it, honestly?

I run a little toy shop and wrote a fable for the kids who come in on Saturdays. Here's how it begins. Would you tell me what you think? "Once there was a clock that was always seven minutes slow, and the town loved it for exactly that reason. Late for church? Blame the clock. Late for love? The clock. It carried the town's small sins like a mule, until the day a clockmaker arrived, tool bag in hand, offering to help."

I make furniture as a hobby and wrote this for my profile. I'd be grateful for any feedback.
"I build furniture slowly, and I'd like to date the same way: sand down only what needs it, leave the grain showing. Weekends I'm in a cold garage with the classical station on. If you'd like to hold the other end of a board and talk about nothing in particular, I'd like that."

I'm a 45-year-old accountant who just started a punk band with two friends from the office. Our chorus:
I carry the one, I carry the two
Carry your lunch order, carry the blame
Tonight I'm carrying nothing but a guitar
And my own goddamn name
What's your take? Please be straight with me.

I'm a bike mechanic, and I want to open a repair cart outside the train station. You drop your bike at 8 a.m. with a tag that lists the issues, and I text you a quote before 9. If you reply "yes," it's done by 5:30, and you pick it up on your way home. If you reply "no," it's free of charge to wait. No shop rent, just a cart and a trailer. What do you think about this idea?

I'm a hobby woodworker, and I'm turning my workshop into a Saturday-morning cafe. The name I've chosen is "Dovetail," for the joint that holds because of how the pieces fit together, like neighbors. What's your take on it?

I'm a retired schoolteacher with an 8-inch telescope, and I posted this in my astronomy club's group: "Saturn tonight from the back garden. The rings were so sharp I could see the Cassini gap. I woke my wife to look. She said, 'It looks fake.' I said, 'That's the nicest thing anyone's said about it.'" Just a bit of fun, but I'd like your opinion.

until it sounds mine

I'm 20, a sophomore working at a campus café. Monthly money is $1,150. Room 520; groceries 180 (Sunday batch cooking); phone 25; textbook fund 50; laundry 20; coffee and friends 80; savings 100; tuition-gap fund 100; clothes 25; unassigned 50. First budget I've ever made. Does it look okay to you? Any advice appreciated!
Hello, I'm a baker and just opened a sourdough place in my town. I'm putting this on the paper bags: "Three days to make. Ten minutes to vanish." Could you tell me your opinion?

Mom of three, so my workouts ride on existing routines. Mon: while the pasta boils, 3 rounds of 10 squats and 10 counter push-ups. Tue: school-run walk, pushing the stroller up the big hill. Wed: during swim lessons, 30 laps. Thu: 20-minute kettlebell video while the kids watch a show. Fri: 15-minute kitchen dance party. Sat: family hike carrying the youngest. Sun: rest. Does this seem sustainable?

I'm 81 and this is the first poem I've ever shown anyone. My granddaughter set up this chat for me. I'd be glad to hear what you think.
At eighty I price the stairs by breath:
the fourth one costs a nickel,
the ninth, a dime.
I reach the landing, solvent still,
and spend what's left on the window.

I'm a student and wrote a short poem for my Instagram, kind of nervous to ask but what do you think? "My grandmother counts in two languages: / Polish for coins and stairs, / English for the days since Dziadek, / and for the rosary, no language, / only the click of the next bead."

I'm a volunteer firefighter and this is my pitch for a side business: "We sell rural fire departments a $4,000-a-year subscription that replaces paper pre-incident plans with drone-mapped 3D layouts of every farm, so crews know where the anhydrous ammonia tank and the old propane shed are before the truck arrives." Be honest, what's your take?

Hello, I'm a brewer starting Low Tide Brewing. The logo is a pint glass in outline. The foam line at the top is a flat horizon, and below it, the beer is filled with faint sand ripples, the pattern left on a beach when the water goes out. One line weight throughout, cream on navy. I'd really like your take on it.

I teach high school drama and I'm writing a musical about a stagehand. This is her big chorus:
Somebody's got to stand in the dark
So the star can find her mark
I'm the tape on the floor, the ghost light's spark
I'm the reason you won't fall
And I'm not in the program at all
I'd love your opinion before I show the cast.
