units: As a new mom going back to school, I'm writing about lullabies. My thesis: "Lullabies across cultures are strikingly dark, with falling cradles and wolves at the door, because they soothe not through content but by letting the parent perform her own anxiety for the infant in a safe, rhythmic, controlled form." I'd love to hear what you think.

Here's one I've been saving for my chess club's newsletter: "My chess rating is like my houseplants: technically alive, and no one is sure why." I'm pretty nervous about sharing it since some of those guys are brutal. How would you rate it?

I've gardened the same plot for six years. My app idea is a journal that learns your microclimate. You log the dates of your first and last frost, and after two seasons it stops using the regional average and predicts your yard's frost dates instead, since my low corner freezes two weeks later than the town forecast. What do you think of this?

Here's my logline. I'm a long-haul trucker, 50, and I write in the cab at rest stops: "With six hours to his deadline, a trucker picks up a hitchhiker who can tell him exactly how many miles he has left to live, and it's fewer than the distance to his daughter's wedding." Thoughts?

I'm a freelance designer and invoice clients in installments. This shows what each client still owes. I aggregated billed and paid separately first so the joins don't multiply rows:
WITH b AS (SELECT client_id, SUM(amount) AS billed FROM invoices GROUP BY 1),
p AS (SELECT i.client_id, SUM(pay.amount) AS paid FROM payments pay JOIN invoices i ON i.id = pay.invoice_id GROUP BY 1)
SELECT c.name, COALESCE(b.billed, 0) - COALESCE(p.paid, 0) AS owed
FROM clients c LEFT JOIN b ON b.client_id = c.id LEFT JOIN p ON p.client_id = c.id
ORDER BY owed DESC;
Thoughts?

Here's my thesis for my music studies seminar, would appreciate your feedback: "Hip-hop sampling is best understood not as theft or homage but as citation: producers like J Dilla built arguments out of other records the way scholars build them out of footnotes." Where would you push me next?

I make a true crime podcast about small towns, called Dead Air. The logo is an audio waveform running across the width of the square. The peaks on the left are shaped like rooftops, a steeple, a water tower, a gabled barn, and then the line goes completely flat for the right third. White on charcoal. I'm a bit nervous posting this. How does it read to you?

I'm captain of our school robotics club, and we got knocked out in round two. Tomorrow I'm speaking to the team: "Our arm dropped the cube at 1:12. I've watched the footage nine times. The arm wasn't the problem; our calibration sheet hadn't been updated since October. So every Friday, someone tests what we assume. Losing in round two taught us more than winning round one would have." How does it read?

I'm 31 and my mother, a seamstress for 45 years, retired Friday. I said: 'Mum has hemmed trousers for brides' fathers, funeral dresses for widows, and one very surprised mayor. She never says she fixes clothes. She says she gives people the right amount of themselves. Mum, you've spent decades letting out other people's seams. Today we let out yours: go be as large as you like.' Honest thoughts?

units: I keep bees, and I sell honey at the farmers' market, so I mapped a forage plan for my 1-acre lot. A six-foot hedge of serviceberry and pussy willow sits in front of the hives to force a high flight path. I'm a grad student who writes songs to cope with deadlines. This chorus is about my grandfather's radio, which I still keep on my desk. Does it work as a chorus, in your view?
He tuned it by feel, a quarter inch of static,
found the ballgame in the hiss like a man finding a door.
Now it sits on my desk, picking up nothing,
but I turn the dial anyway. I just want to hear it once more.

Monthly cohort retention for our subscription app. I'm a data scientist and wrote it in one sitting, so tell me if I've missed something.
WITH f AS (
  SELECT customer_id, MIN(date_trunc('month', ordered_at)) AS cohort
  FROM orders GROUP BY 1)
SELECT f.cohort,
  DATEDIFF('month', f.cohort, date_trunc('month', o.ordered_at)) AS months_since,
  COUNT(DISTINCT o.customer_id) AS active
FROM f JOIN orders o USING (customer_id)
GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1, 2;

Retired baker, still experimenting. Rye and caraway sourdough discard crackers: 150g discard, 60g rye flour, 40g olive oil, 1 tsp salt, 1 tsp caraway seeds. Mix, rest 30 minutes, roll paper thin, brush with water, and sprinkle with flaky salt and more seeds. Bake at 180°C for 18 minutes, rotating once, until they're deep amber and snap. I'd like a second opinion, please.

I run a used bookshop and wrote a jazzy little number about it. Here's the chorus. I'd be curious about your reaction, whatever it is.

a train ride, a bathtub, a borrowed flashlight.
I just keep the kettle on and the lamp lit low,
and the dead keep writing to whoever's up.

units: I own a used bookstore, and my clerk Miriam retires after 21 years. Draft of my toast: "Miriam can look at a stranger for three seconds and hand them the book they didn't know they were missing. I've watched her do it nine hundred times and never seen her wrong. She'd call it luck. I call it a kind of love. We stock forty thousand books. Miriam, you were the one worth recommending." Feedback?

Here's my thesis for my music studies seminar, would appreciate your feedback: "Hip-hop sampling is best understood not as theft or homage but as citation: producers like J Dilla built arguments out of other records the way scholars build them out of footnotes." Where would you push me next?

I run a small bakery and I'm mentoring a student with this idea. Sourdough starter in identical clear jars, same flour and hydration, held at 18, 22, 26 and 30°C in water baths. Time-lapse photos mark rise height every 10 minutes. Then we compute peak-rise time and estimate Q10 for fermentation. Three jars per temperature. How would you rate the approach?

I run a tiny karaoke bar in Manila and I've been turning my regulars into a script. Logline: "Every Thursday for eleven years, a stranger has sung the same ballad at a karaoke bar; when he stops coming, the tone-deaf owner learns the song and sets out to find him." Thoughts?

I dispatch buses and write short emails. This one's for my manager. Opinion?
"Hi Pat, route 14's 7:40 is always 8 minutes late because the school crossing on Elm adds traffic. Drivers have logged it for three weeks. Move the timetable to 7:48 and the complaint calls stop. It costs nothing. Thanks, Ruth."

I'm a vet tech, and kids ask me about death all the time. Premise: Gus's goldfish dies, and at the funeral each relative gives a different eulogy. Gran's is wrong, Dad's is too short, and Gus slowly realizes each of them knew a different fish. Last line: "Gus said his own, and it was the longest." Could you give me your opinion?

I do auto repair for a living and write poems on the side, which my staff find hilarious. Here's one:
Customer says it makes a noise
but only when she isn't there.
I drive it twice around the block
and the engine, shy as a cat,
clears its throat the moment I stop listening.
What do you think?

I farm a few acres and write stories in the winter. Here's the beginning of one, if you'd give me your honest reaction: "Ma used to say the wind in Dry Fork had opinions. The morning it started whispering our names one by one, I figured it had finally made up its mind about us. Pa ignored it. Pa had ignored most things, including the well, which had been dry since March and had the manners to be quiet about it."

I'm a club chess player, 52, and I blog about my games. This one's titled "I Lost to an Eight-Year-Old and Here's the Move That Did It." It begins: "She pushed her h-pawn on move six, I laughed, and for the next forty minutes I learned that being amused is the most expensive mistake in chess." Honest feedback welcome!

first paragraph of my letter for the Alder Street community garden, be gentle lol: "Mrs. Okafor planted the first tomato here in 2009, in a lot that held a burned-out Buick. Sixteen summers later, forty families eat from it. The water main beneath it is failing, and replacing it costs $11,200. We're asking you to help keep the tomatoes coming." Thoughts?

Could you tell me what you think?

I'm a marine biologist and I'm starting a company called Shell Game. We pick up oyster shells from restaurants weekly, a fee of $30 a month, cure them for six months and deliver them to reef restoration projects. Each restaurant receives a plaque: "Your shells built 3 square feet of reef." Photos and GPS coordinates are included each quarter. Would restaurants actually pay? Curious what you think.

I do open mics on Thursdays as a hobby, and this is my new opener: "I slept wrong once in 2019 and my neck is still in litigation." I'm tempted to follow it with nothing, just let it sit. Does that instinct make sense? Genuinely curious.

I'm an undergrad raising $3,000 to sequence soil from my grandmother's farm. Here's my opening, and I'm a bit anxious about it: "My grandmother says the south field is tired. I study microbes, so I asked what tired means. A teaspoon of that soil holds billions of organisms, and I'd like to find out which ones have quit." How does it land for you?
For my marketing class I invented an alarm clock that wakes you with gradual sunlight. My slogan is "Sunrise, minus the rooster." Can you give me feedback? My professor wants peer opinions.

Because I forget things, my budget is automated on payday (TA income $1,700). Rent $720 and utilities $55 autopay; $200 auto-savings; $60 'forgetful tax' fund for late fees and lost stuff; groceries $250; phone $35; transit $70; books $60; $200 weekly cash envelopes ($50 × 4) for fun; $50 buffer. What do you think of the system?

units: I've been a landlord for 15 years, and I've seen too many deposit fights. My app idea is Day One. At move-in, tenant and landlord walk through together. The app guides them room by room, with a required photo of each wall, floor and appliance. Each photo is timestamped and cryptographically hashed. At the end, both sign and get the same PDF. Would tenants actually use this? What do you think?

I'm a grad student, writing a short story about my grandmother. Sharing the first paragraph with some nerves: "The telegram came on a Tuesday, which my grandmother held against Tuesdays for the rest of her life. She forgave the postman, the war, and eventually God. But Tuesdays she kept, the way a dog keeps a bone, and so for sixty years, every week, we ate cold supper and did not answer the door." What do you think?

I own a tiny skate shop and I'm not great at talking about myself, but here's my attempt. What do you think?
"I sell skateboards to teenagers and have been told 'that's cringe' by every one of them. I'm 31, I still eat it on ledges, and I keep a first aid kit in my truck for exactly that reason. Looking for someone who'll film my attempts and not post the bad ones."

I'm a plumber and I came up with this for the side of my van: "Every house has one pipe that's been quietly holding a grudge since 1974." My wife says it's too long for a van. Be straight with me: would you read it, and would you call me?

Hi! For my nursing capstone I came up with this: "Among night-shift nurses on medical-surgical wards, does a protected 20-minute nap during breaks reduce medication administration errors in the final three hours of shift compared with caffeine alone?" I'm a bit nervous about showing my advisor. Thoughts?

I'm in an MFA program and workshopping this next week. Before I do, I'd like a fresh reader's take, especially on the line breaks:
The heron holds the river's one idea
so still the water starts to doubt itself.
Then the small bright argument
of a minnow, and the whole grey sentence
resolves into a throat.

i'm in 8th grade and my teacher said to pick a problem at our school. my thesis is: "Our cafeteria throws away about forty pounds of untouched food daily, and the cause isn't picky eaters but a twenty-minute lunch period that ends before students finish, so lunch should be lengthened before any composting program is considered." what do you think?

I'm a divorce lawyer, and I write romance on the side under a pen name. Here's my opening line: "The custody agreement gave Dev the house and Priya the sourdough starter, and neither of them, in the end, knew how to keep the thing alive." How does it read to you?

Just finished this chorus and I'm kind of buzzing, so I'm sharing it right away. I'm a senior in high school, and it's about my town. Tell me what you think!
Everybody here knows my middle name and my mother's,
the truck my dad sold, the fence I drove through.
I'm leaving in June with one bag and no one's blessing.
God, I hope someplace else knows me half as well as you.

I'm opening a cafe that only runs from 8pm until 3am, for night owls, insomniacs and shift workers. The name is "Moth & Ember." Moths come to the light, embers keep glowing after the fire's gone, and that's the mood I want. I'm 31 and a former bartender. Does the name give you the right picture?

units: I'm a nursing student, and I was asked to say a few words for Carol, a night-shift nurse retiring after 38 years: "Carol taught me that 3 a.m. is when patients tell the truth. Hold the hand, she said, lower the lights, and wait. Thirty-eight years of waiting with strangers so they weren't alone. I may never be as good, but I'll be awake, and that was the first thing she taught me." Honest opinion?

As a new mom going back to school, I'm writing about lullabies. My thesis: "Lullabies across cultures are strikingly dark, with falling cradles and wolves at the door, because they soothe not through content but by letting the parent perform her own anxiety for the infant in a safe, rhythmic, controlled form." I'd love to hear what you think.

I teach physics and I'm opening our astronomy society's autumn meeting with this. "Vega's light left in the year our newest member was born, so tonight, when you look up, you're seeing Vega as a toddler. Every observing night is time travel with bad coffee. Bring a flask, bring a child, and let's go meet the past together." Could you tell me what you make of it?

After 30 years as a newspaper reporter, I'm opening a cafe in the old Gazette building, and I'm calling it "Stop Press." The menu will be printed on broadsheet and the coffee will be strong enough to meet a deadline. Does the name have the right ring to it? Tell me straight, I've had worse feedback from editors.

I translate Korean webtoons as a fan hobby, and I'm applying for a junior localization job. This is my cover letter paragraph on translation philosophy. What do you make of it?
"In one series, a character says '밥 먹었어?' to mean 'I love you.' A literal translation says 'Did you eat?' A faithful one says something else entirely. I've learned to keep the question and add the worry around it: 'Have you eaten yet? You look tired.'"

I drive the Route 9 bus and write poems on my breaks. This is from the last run of the night. What do you think?
Route 9, final run. The bus exhales.
Rows of seats keep the shapes of strangers,
a dent here, a warmth there,
and I drive the empty ghosts back to the depot
with my headlights on for them.

We run a small vegetable farm with a CSA of 60 members. My idea: members can swap items in their box until Wednesday night, like trading kale for extra carrots. The app then sends us a harvest list adjusted by swaps, so we pick what's wanted. It also shows a 'surplus' list for cheap add-ons. Could you tell me what you think?

Hey, I'm a 45-year-old pediatric nurse, and I wrote this for a short film contest: "When a ten-year-old's imaginary friend begins aging faster than she does, she has one childhood left to keep him alive." Does it work as a logline? Any feedback welcome.

I'm 61 and a member of our amateur radio club. I'm giving a short talk at the anniversary evening. Could you give me your opinion? "At 2 a.m., someone in Tasmania heard my call sign and replied, 'Good evening, Yorkshire.' Four watts, a wire in my loft, and the curvature of the Earth politely stepping aside. In a world of billions of messages, I still love the thirty seconds when two strangers agree to listen."

I'm a weekend woodworker and I'm demoing at our makerspace open house. I'm opening with: "This chair has no screws, no nails, and no glue. It's held together by nothing but the fact that wood shrinks." Just wondering how that sounds to you. Be as blunt as you like!

units: Just graduated and applying for backend jobs. This is the first bullet under my internship: "Reduced p95 checkout API latency from 1.8s to 310ms by replacing N+1 Postgres queries with batched lookups and adding a read-through Redis cache, saving an estimated $42K/yr in compute." What do you think? Anything you'd change?

I'm an occupational therapist, and this is my layout for a sensory garden in a dementia care home. A looped path, 1.5m wide, with no dead ends, so no one gets stuck. Along it, five stations: scent (lavender, rosemary), touch (lamb's ear, grasses), sound (bamboo, wind chimes), taste (raspberries, mint) and a familiar-memory corner with a washing line and a shed. Handrails run along the edges, and the seating is every 12m. Would you give me your thoughts?

I'm a 62-year-old dairy farmer. At my neighbor Walt's retirement, I said: 'Walt farmed the same hundred and sixty acres as his father. People call that standing still. But I watched him walk that fence line every morning for forty years, and the ground under him changed more than any of us did. You don't stay in one place by not moving. You stay by tending.' Honest feedback welcome.

I'm 72 and I've sewn for fifty years. My idea is adaptive clothing alterations. I'd convert people's own favorite shirts and trousers with magnetic buttons, side-opening seams and soft tags, for people with arthritis or limited mobility. My slogan is: "Keep the shirt you love. Change how it opens." I charge $18 per garment. I'm a little shy about putting this out there. Please tell me what you think.

I'm 80 and my granddaughter said I should show someone. It's a story from my childhood, dressed up a bit:
"The summer I was nine, the circus came to Ballina and left without its elephant. Nobody could explain it. She stood in Mr. Doyle's field for six weeks, enormous and patient, eating his hay, until the whole parish had told her something it had never told another living soul."
What do you think, dear?

I'm a college freshman, and my aunt Rosa is retiring from our family farm. I'm giving the speech: "Aunt Rosa gets up at 4:30 because the cows don't read calendars. I used to think that was sad. Now I think it's the most honest schedule I know: someone needs you, so you show up. Forty years, no vacations, a full table every Sunday. Rosa, rest. The cows will understand. We won't, but we'll try." Thoughts?

History major here, posted this thread opener and I'm hoping for honest feedback: "The Library of Alexandria didn't burn in one dramatic night. It faded the way libraries do: budgets cut, scholars leaving, scrolls not recopied. Knowledge is lost less like a bonfire and more like a slow leak. Worth remembering when we trim library hours."

I'm a freelance-turned-staff designer and the rebrand has ballooned. Does this email to my manager work?
"Hi Jo, the rebrand has grown from 6 deliverables to 14 since kickoff. All reasonable asks, but at my pace it lands three weeks late. Options: cut the packaging mockups, bring in Rafi for 10 days, or move the deadline to 21 June. I lean toward Rafi. Which do you prefer?"

I work nights as a nurse and write on my breaks. Bit nervous to show anyone. This is how my story begins:
"The patient in bed nine had been dying politely for three weeks. He thanked us for the blankets, apologised for the trouble, and every night at three asked, very gently, whether we'd mind not letting the other man in. There was no other man. Bed ten was empty."
Honest thoughts?

Hi! For my nursing capstone I came up with this: "Among night-shift nurses on medical-surgical wards, does a protected 20-minute nap during breaks reduce medication administration errors in the final three hours of shift compared with caffeine alone?" I'm a bit nervous about showing my advisor. Thoughts?

units: My partner and I are saving for a house. Combined take-home $9,800: rent 2,400; groceries 700; utilities 220; transit 300; insurance 180; house fund 2,500; index funds 1,800; dining and fun 900; travel 500; giving 300. Rule: if any category overspends, it borrows from fun, never from the house fund. What's your opinion?

I'm a 1600-rated club chess player writing up a project for fun. My question: "For players rated 1400 to 1800 in 15+10 online games, do time-trouble blunders cost more rating points than opening errors, and does that balance shift after a player's first thirty games?" I'd use Lichess data. Would love any opinion you have!

I'm a 31-year-old firefighter preparing for our annual physical agility test. Mon: stair climbs in a 20 kg vest, 5x3 minutes. Tue: sled drags 6x20 m, farmer carries 4x40 m. Wed: 40-minute easy run. Thu: cable hose-pull simulation 5x30 s, dummy drags. Fri: heavy deadlifts 5x3. Sat: full timed test circuit. Sun: rest, foam roll. Does this seem right to you?

I'm a chess club coach opening a quick takeaway cafe next to the park tables where people play. I'd like to name it "En Passant," the chess capture made in passing. Is the name clear and appealing to you? Be candid.

I'm a nursing student and I blog about clinicals. Here's my latest title and first sentence: "What the Night Shift Taught Me Before I Had a License." "At 3 a.m. on my first rotation, a patient who hadn't spoken all week asked me to open the window, and I understood that half of nursing is noticing what people can't bring themselves to request." Thoughts? Anything you'd change?

Hi! I play chess competitively as a hobby, and I'm toasting two fellow club members. Here goes: "In chess, we say the opening is theory, the middlegame is imagination, and the endgame is technique. Raj and Claire skipped the opening, played a wildly imaginative middlegame in the club parking lot, and now they're in an endgame where the only rule is that nobody resigns. May every draw be by agreement. To Raj and Claire." Thoughts?
I'm 10 and I made up a joke for my class talent show. What did the clock say when it got sent to the principal? "I was only tocking." My mum says I should ask someone else. What do you think?

Long-time fantasy reader, first-time writer here. My novel begins: "Tuesday was the day Thornwick hid its children, so the dragon's tax collector found only goats, a very old man, and an unusually loud silence." Would you tell me what you think? Be gentle, I'm a bit anxious about this.

I'm applying for a historical marker for the old Delmar Bakery on 5th Street. Our statement opens: "For 41 years this building fed the neighborhood on credit. A ledger still hangs on the back wall, recording striking miners' debts the owner never collected. Towns are remembered for their monuments, but they're held together by their bakeries." How does it read to you?

I'm a 34-year-old bus driver. I came up with Ramp Request. A rider at a stop opens the app and taps one button, "I need the ramp." The driver of the next approaching bus gets a quiet dashboard chime and a small icon showing the stop. Nobody has to wave or talk, and the driver can pull in at the right spot. I've pitched it to nobody yet. What's your take?

units: I'm a linguistics major, and my idea is menu rewrites for immigrant-owned restaurants. I'm a college freshman, and my aunt Rosa is retiring from our family farm. I'm giving the speech: "Aunt Rosa gets up at 4:30 because the cows don't read calendars. I used to think that was sad. Now I think it's the most honest schedule I know: someone needs you, so you show up. Forty years, no vacations, a full table every Sunday. Rosa, rest. The cows will understand. We won't, but we'll try." Thoughts?

I'm a structural engineer. My app idea is CrackCheck. You put a printed 5 cm reference card next to a wall crack and photograph it. Computer vision measures the width to about 0.1 mm. Every month it reminds you to re-shoot from the same angle, using a ghost overlay of the last photo. If the width grows more than 0.3 mm, it tells you to call a professional. Thoughts?
For my marketing class I invented an alarm clock that wakes you with gradual sunlight. My slogan is "Sunrise, minus the rooster." Can you give me feedback? My professor wants peer opinions.

I moved here from Vietnam eight years ago. My idea is Backpack Letter. You photograph any school letter or form. It tells you in Vietnamese, or another language you choose, what the letter is about, what you have to do, and the deadline. Then it adds the deadline to your calendar, with a reminder two days before. It never translates word for word. It says things like "They need a signature, not money." I'd like your opinion.

I'm a junior in chemistry and I'm putting together a pitch for a competition. Here's my one sentence: "Universities auction off decommissioned lab equipment for pennies, so we recondition and calibrate it, certify it, and sell forty-year-old spectrometers to high school and community college labs at a tenth of the price of new." Any feedback?

My grandmother actually ran a dry cleaner, which inspired this. "A Korean grandmother who has worked in a Brooklyn dry cleaner for thirty years is the only witness who can identify a killer, but she has spent those years pretending not to speak English." Does this work for you? I'd love to hear your opinion.

We run a small vegetable farm with a CSA of 60 members. My idea: members can swap items in their box until Wednesday night, like trading kale for extra carrots. The app then sends us a harvest list adjusted by swaps, so we pick what's wanted. It also shows a 'surplus' list for cheap add-ons. Could you tell me what you think?

I'm a 20-year-old intern and somehow I was asked to speak for our founder. I said: 'I've known Mr. Reyes for eleven weeks. In that time he learned my name, my coffee order, and the name of my cat. I'm told he also started a company. I'll take people's word for it. But anyone who remembers the intern's cat has already built something that lasts.' Was that too bold?

I'm a marine biologist and I'm starting a company called Shell Game. We pick up oyster shells from restaurants weekly, a fee of $30 a month, cure them for six months and deliver them to reef restoration projects. Each restaurant receives a plaque: "Your shells built 3 square feet of reef." Photos and GPS coordinates are included each quarter. Would restaurants actually pay? Curious what you think.

Week 10 of my marathon block, aiming for 3:15. Mon: rest, 15 minutes of yoga. Tue: 8x400 m at 5k pace, 90 s jog. Wed: 10 km easy plus 6 strides. Thu: 16 km with 8 km at marathon pace (4:37/km). I'm a student who works at a skate rink, and I spotted a hazard. This is my email to my manager:
"Hi Joan, the rubber mat by the rental counter has curled at one corner. Two kids tripped on it today, and nobody was hurt. I've put an orange cone on it and taken a photo, attached. A replacement is about $40 at the hardware store on Elm, and I can pick it up on my way in tomorrow. Okay to do that? Thanks, Sam"
What do you think?

Pareto analysis for our catalogue: what share of revenue the top products make. I added the tie-breaker and ROWS frame deliberately.
WITH r AS (SELECT product_id, SUM(revenue) AS rev FROM sales GROUP BY product_id)
SELECT product_id, rev,
  SUM(rev) OVER (ORDER BY rev DESC, product_id ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) / SUM(rev) OVER () AS cum_share
FROM r ORDER BY rev DESC, product_id;
I'm a finance manager, not a developer. Does this look right to you?

I'm a retired electrician and this is my first poem since school. I wrote it about my mother's house:
I rewired my mother's house in 1987.
Behind the plaster, still, her wedding year:
cloth-wrapped cable, brittle as old licorice,
still carrying, without complaint,
the little the house had asked of it.
What would you say to it, honestly?

"The map was wrong in the way maps are wrong when they love you: it left out the cliff, the wolves, the long unfashionable middle of the journey, and drew the sea closer than it was. Imre followed it anyway. You can forgive a lot in something that wanted you to arrive."
How does it come across?

Here's my bullet: "Rerouted a 40-truck fleet using a weather- and traffic-weighted spreadsheet model I built, cutting deadhead miles 17% and saving about 31,000 gallons of diesel per year." Mind giving me your opinion?

Does this make sense? Roast me if needed.

I own a café and wanted to automate our happy-hour pricing, including our late-night window. Here's my function. Thoughts?
```python
def in_window(now, start, end):
    """True if now is in [start, end), even across midnight."""
    if start <= end:
        return start <= now < end
    return now >= start or now < end
```

I run a chess club and I'm giving a talk to new members. I start with: "Chess is just like life, because in both there are moves." I think it sets the tone. Thoughts?

Like Shakespeare once said in Hamlet, 'To be or not to be funded.' Without a roof, theater will be gone forever. Help us today!" Let me know what you think.
